## ChatGPT 测评：GPT-6 时代的「全家桶」，唯一让我犹豫的是那个带广告的 Go 档

发表时间：2026-10-31 20:12

AI TRENDS HUB · 工具测评 · 2026-10

ChatGPT 测评：GPT-6 时代的「全家桶」，唯一让我犹豫的是那个带广告的 Go 档

免费档给得越来越大方，付费档却在悄悄分层——2026 年 10 月的 ChatGPT，更像一个平台而不是一个聊天框。

先说结论

如果只允许装一个 AI 应用，我还是会选 ChatGPT——不是因为它每个单项都最强，而是因为它是唯一一个把对话、图像、语音、代码、深度研究、定时任务全部塞进同一个账号的产品。但这次测评我最想聊的不是它有多强，而是它的套餐结构正在发生一件值得警惕的事：OpenAI 开始用「广告」来区分付费档位了。

这半年最大的变化：GPT-6 落地，套餐变成四档

打开官网定价页，第一眼就能确认 GPT-6 已经全面铺开：免费档直接标注「GPT-6 文字对话次数不限」。这句话值得多看一眼——在 GPT-4 时代，免费用户用的是落后一代的模型；现在 OpenAI 把最新模型的文字对话敞开了，限制转移到了上传、图像生成、语音、深度研究和 Codex 这些「高成本功能」上。对只拿它聊天、改文案的人来说，免费档比两年前厚道得多。

付费档现在是三层：Go、Plus、Pro。这次访问时官网按地区自动切换成了韩元标价：Go 每月 ₩13,000，Plus ₩29,000，Pro 起价 ₩159,000。按当日汇率折算，Plus 约合 20 美元，和美元区公开报价（Plus $20/月、Pro 起 $100/月）基本吻合，说明 OpenAI 没有做地区歧视定价。

▲ ChatGPT 官方定价页（2026-10-29 抓取）。官网按访问地区自动切换货币，本次显示为韩元。（chatgpt.com 定价页）

▲ ChatGPT 四档套餐价格对比。免费档给的是最新模型的文字对话，付费档解锁的是高成本功能。（图表：基于官方数据换算）

Go 档的「可能包含广告」，是今年 AI 付费模式的一个信号

仔细看 Go 档的说明，有一句很容易被滑过去的话：「此套餐可能包含广告。」付费套餐里塞广告，这在主流 AI 产品里是第一次。月付 ₩13,000（约 9 美元）买的是「更多消息、更多上传、更多图像、更长记忆」，但你仍然要看广告。Plus 档才把这层广告摘掉，同时给 GPT-6 的高级推理模型、项目、计划任务和自定义 GPT。

我的判断是：Go 档的定位根本不是给个人用户升级用的，它是给「免费用户里用量大的那批人」准备的缓冲带——用便宜的价格把你从免费池里捞出来，同时用广告覆盖推理成本。如果你已经在认真考虑付费，直接跳过 Go 看 Plus，省下的 11 美元不值得用广告来换。

Pro 档真正的卖点不是模型，是「Dot」

Pro 起价 ₩159,000（约 110 美元），页面列出的差异项里，最值得注意的是一个叫「Dot，你的全天候智能体」的东西，以及「Codex 和 ChatGPT 工作的会话时长更长」。GPT-6 Astra 专业推理当然重要，但推理能力的差距对普通文档工作已经越来越不敏感；一个 24 小时挂着、能替你跑长任务的 agent，才是 OpenAI 想把 Pro 卖到三倍价格的理由。页面同时注明 Pro 分 3 档用量，却只标了「起价」——具体档差要登录后才能看到，这种透明度说实话不够。

▲ 十款工具最低可用付费档对比。ChatGPT Plus 处在 $20 的主流价位带，但它的免费档是这批产品里给得最多的。（图表：基于官方数据换算）

缺点，说三个实在的

功能堆得太密。侧边栏里聊天、图像、Codex、深度研究、ChatGPT 工作、GPT 商店挤在一起，新用户第一周大概率找不到「计划任务」藏在哪。

Pro 的 3 档用量不透明。官网只写「起价」不写具体数字，意味着你要付完钱才知道自己买的是哪一档。

Sora 消费级 App 在今年 4 月停运之后，ChatGPT 内置的视频能力明显收缩，如果你冲着「一个订阅包打所有模态」来的，视频这条腿现在比其他三家都短。

适合谁，不适合谁

适合：想要一个账号解决 80% 日常 AI 需求的人；已经在用 GPT 生态（自定义 GPT、API）的人；团队协作场景（Business 档 $20/席位/年起）。不适合：只想安静写长文的人——那部分需求 Claude 的中文行文更稳；以及重度视频创作者——去 Runway 或者可灵。

评分 8.6/10。扣分主要在套餐透明度和视频短板。结论：默认选项依然是默认选项，但别再闭着眼睛续费了，先想清楚你要的到底是 Plus 还是 Pro——这俩现在是两个产品。

# OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra for desktop automation

Last update: 31/10/2026

Author Isaac

- GPT-6.1 Terra reduces API costs by 50% compared to its previous version.
- It is optimized for computer use, visual reasoning, and office tasks.
- It far surpasses the Sol and Astra models in speed and economic efficiency.
- It shows a drastic reduction in hallucinations and factual errors in its benchmarks.

The OpenAI model family has just taken a significant leap forward with the arrival of GPT-6.1 Terra . This isn't their most powerful model, but rather a tool specifically designed for those who need AI to interact with their computers smoothly, quickly, and, above all, without their API bill skyrocketing at the end of the month.

Essentially, this release fills the gap where you need visual reasoning and office automation without having to pay the premium price of flagship models. It's a direct replacement for the older GPT-5.6 Terra, arriving with efficiency that promises to change how we build our AI agents for everyday tasks.

## What exactly does GPT-6.1 Terra consist of?

To understand where Terra fits in, you have to look at how OpenAI has organized its current catalog. They have a scale that ranges from the simplest to the most complex: Luna, Terra, Sol, and Astra. While Sol and Luna had already jumped to Generation 6 last month, Terra had been stuck at version 5.6 until now. This new jump to version 6.1 brings it up to date and optimizes it for everyday desktop tasks.

What makes this model special is her ability to interpret technical drawings, fill out tedious forms, and manage invoices in accounting software. She's also very good at video editing and writing proposals, always striving for a balance where the writing is natural but the execution is precise and, above all, very cost-effective.

## A major blow to API prices

If there's one thing that's going to make developers smile, it's the cost. OpenAI has cut the standard API prices in half compared to version 5.6 Terra. In fact, it's even cheaper than the GPT-6.1 Sol model, allowing developers to run inference processes in production at a much lower cost.

This price reduction not only affects the API, but is also noticeable in ChatGPT Work and Codex , where the usage quota allows for significantly more tasks than before. It is undoubtedly the logical choice for any company that automates large-scale workflows and wants to optimize its operating costs.

## Performance analysis and benchmarks

Let's be clear: Terra isn't aiming to be the king of pure intelligence rankings, but rather the king of task efficiency . In the Agents' Last Exam tests, which measure proficiency in using work software, Terra pulverizes its predecessor, GPT-5.6, surpassing it by about 15 percentage points while costing barely a third. It even manages to tie with GPT-6 Astra, but at only a tenth of the cost per token.

In terms of speed, the data indicates it's more than three times faster than the Sol and Astra models. For programmers, TerminalBench 4.0 shows a dramatic improvement, jumping from a 21.5% success rate in the previous version to 50.3% task completion with maximum reasoning effort.

Compared to its competitors, specifically Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, OpenAI claims that Terra is three times more token-efficient and costs a quarter of the price, resulting in a cost per task that is approximately nine times lower. However, these figures should be taken with a grain of salt until independent testing is available, as they are based on data provided by the manufacturer.

## Goodbye to hallucinations and improvements in security

Combating factual errors has been OpenAI's top priority this year. In internal tests designed to make the model fail, Terra has managed to reduce its error rate from 53.6% to 16.7% in basic reasoning . When pushed to its limits, the error rate drops to 4.3%, putting it on par with the most expensive models.

Furthermore, the model is now more transparent about its limitations and is more resistant to prompt injection attacks . In terms of security, OpenAI has classified it as "Critical" in its Cybersecurity Readiness Framework. This serves as a warning to those building autonomous agents: don't rely solely on AI and implement effective permission limits on the operating system where it runs.

## Choice guide: Terra, Sol or Astra?

Choosing the right model depends entirely on the complexity of the task. If you need maximum power for heavy engineering, go for the GPT-6 Astra . If your work involves multi-stage programming and deep reasoning where cost is secondary, the GPT-6.1 Sol is your best option.

However, for everything else—document management, forms, and repetitive office tasks— GPT-6.1 Terra is the ideal tool . A smart strategy for developers is to create a routing system: let Terra handle routine tasks and escalate only complex problems to Sol or Astra, thus saving a considerable amount of money.

## Access and startup

This model is already operational for Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu plan users through Codex and ChatGPT Work. Developers can implement it right now using the ID gpt-6.1-terra in the API. To get the most out of it, tools like Eigent, an open-source desktop application, allow you to build a workforce of local agents to execute real-world workflows, from reviewing pull requests on GitHub to automating desktop tasks.

The arrival of this model consolidates a tiered strategy where speed and cost savings allow for the delegation of high-volume tasks to AI without fear of budget constraints. By combining a drastic reduction in factual errors with speed three times faster than top-of-the-range models, OpenAI offers a pragmatic solution for massive enterprise automation.

# Graduate of Asia's second-best university pushes boundaries of AI-generated video at Google DeepMind

Yu, who is a senior research scientist at Google DeepMind, was named to MIT Technology Review's 2026 Innovators Under 35 Asia Pacific list for his contributions to AI systems that can understand and generate videos.

Google DeepMind is the company's AI research division, responsible for developing some of its most advanced AI technologies, including Gemini, its family of AI models, and Veo, its video-generation technology.

From school programming to the forefront of AI research

His interest in programming began in high school, when he wrote a computer program to ring a bell at scheduled times after the school's regular bell system was turned off during exams, according to a profile published by Peking University on Oct. 26.

Although his family encouraged him to study economics, he was more interested in computers. He enrolled at Peking University, where he pursued both subjects and graduated in 2019 with bachelor's degrees in computer science and economics. Peking University ranked second in Asia in both the 2026 QS and Times Higher Education regional university rankings.

Yu initially considered specializing in operating systems but turned to artificial intelligence after encouragement from a professor. In 2018, he joined a summer research program at Carnegie Mellon University in the U.S., where he studied how computers analyze videos. He later pursued doctoral research in the U.S. and worked as a research intern at Google, shifting his focus from teaching AI to understand videos to developing systems that could generate them.

His research led to several major projects, including MAGVIT and MAGVIT-v2, which improved how AI processes and generates images and videos.

He also helped develop VideoPoet, a Google AI system that can create videos from written instructions, animate still images and edit existing footage. The research won a Best Paper Award at the 2024 International Conference on Machine Learning, a major international AI research conference.

Yu Lijun, research scientist at Google DeepMind. Photo courtesy of Peking University

Yu joined Google DeepMind as a senior research scientist in May 2024, according to his professional CV. He has contributed to several major projects, including Gemini, Veo 3.1 and Nano Banana, an AI tool that allows users to create and edit images.

Despite AI's rapid advances, he believes researchers should focus on problems that genuinely interest them rather than simply following the latest technological trends. He also emphasizes the importance of scientific rigor, arguing that researchers remain responsible for ensuring their findings are reliable, regardless of how much AI assists their work.

For students considering a career in AI, he offers a question: "When the AI buzz eventually fizzles out, would you still want to research it?"

# 谷歌DeepMind用模拟患者训练Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite，精神科问诊急性风险漏报率从30.5%降至12.9%

BitMart Insights | 2026.10.31 15:34

1 分钟 阅读时间

谷歌 DeepMind 的研究人员让一个小型 Gemini 模型经历了一场类似精神科住院医师培训的过程。在 2026 年 10 月 29 日发布的一篇预印本中，他们报告称，用模拟患者对 Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite 进行训练，显著改善了其开展精神科问诊访谈的表现。

最受关注的是安全性数字。在对抗性测试中，该模型未能升级上报的急性安全风险比例从此前的 30.5% 降至 12.9%。

研究人员实际测试了什么

论文题为《Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake》（arXiv:2610.40476），对 Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite 应用了多轮强化学习。模型与模拟患者对话，获得评分，然后据此调整。

为评估结果，团队开展了一项随机、双盲、交叉设计的客观结构化临床考试（OSCE）。32 名获得委员会认证的精神科医生在不知情的情况下，对经强化学习训练的智能体与基线模型进行配对比较。

受训智能体在这些配对比较中胜出 76.7%，报告 p 值低于 0.0001。

提升体现在精神科医生评分的多个维度：

- 联盟与沟通：受训智能体 82.0%，基线模型 65.2%
- 诊断适当性：68.3% 对 33.3%
- 病史采集、鉴别诊断、处置方案与文书记录均有改善

在 127 个经精神科医生验证的场景中，受训智能体的临床评分表得分从 0.379 升至 0.706。

最关键的安全性测试

漏诊（under-triage）数据来自 256 个围绕标准化安全风险分类构建的对抗性场景。基线模型有 30.5% 的情况未能升级上报急性风险，训练后该比例降至 12.9%，p 值同样低于 0.0001。

这项工作将 DeepMind 此前建立的 ResidencyRL 框架扩展到了精神科领域。一个核心设计选择是分层奖励系统，对优先级进行排序，把临床能力与安全指标并列考量。

该研究还刻意选用了一款轻量级模型。Flash-Lite 处于 Gemini 系列中更小、更便宜的一端。

这对医疗 AI 意味着什么

有几个明确的局限值得关注。这是一篇预印本，研究结果尚未完成正式同行评审，而且所有测试都在模拟与考试环境中进行，而非真实患者。

在对抗性场景中把漏诊率降至 12.9% 是一项强有力的研究结果，但任何在重要医疗护理场景中的部署，想必都需要人类监督以及多得多的验证。

32 名精神科医生在不知评分对象身份的情况下，始终选择了受训模型。

# Google's Gemini 4 Carbon AI Model Poised to Slash Startup Costs

Google's new "Gemini 4 Carbon" model is set to redefine startup opportunities by automating programming and cybersecurity, significantly reducing digital product development costs. This launch intensifies the competition among AI giants.

6 min read

Artificial intelligence is entering a new phase of competition, no longer limited to generating text and answering queries, but extending to independently executing complex programming and engineering tasks. Google is banking on this with its new Gemini 4 Carbon model, which aims to accelerate digital product development, improve operational efficiency, and open new opportunities for startups to develop technological solutions without the traditional burdens of establishing large technical teams.

Google DeepMind, part of the Alphabet group, announced the model's launch on October 28, 2026, with a focus on developing Agentic AI capabilities. This allows the model to handle multi-stage tasks, analyze problems, work on code, and debug large codebases, rather than merely offering suggestions or instructions to the user.

The launch of Gemini 4 Carbon reflects the global tech companies' trend towards developing systems capable of completing integrated tasks, enhancing their potential application in software, fintech, e-commerce, and cybersecurity sectors. It also provides startups with additional tools to accelerate product development, potentially reducing the time and resources needed to reach markets.

## Google DeepMind Leads Model Development

Gemini 4 Carbon is a product of Google DeepMind, which operates under the Alphabet umbrella and is a key pillar of the group's strategy for developing advanced AI models.

Google was founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin, while Google DeepMind was formed in its current structure in 2023, following the merger of DeepMind and Google Brain, to develop a number of advanced models and applications within the group's ecosystem.

The model is based on the concept of Agentic AI, which involves treating a task as a series of interconnected steps, executing them, reviewing results, and addressing problems that arise during the work, with the ability to continue handling complex engineering projects for extended periods.

Google states that its internal teams tested Gemini 4 Carbon's ability to work for days on multi-stage engineering tasks, including identifying root causes of errors and fixing subtle issues within large codebases and low-level systems, which expands its scope of use compared to tools limited to responding to direct commands.

## Cybersecurity and Programming at the Forefront of Capabilities

Programming and cybersecurity are the primary areas of focus for Google's new model. Gemini 4 Carbon scored 88.2% in the SEC-bench Pro test for vulnerability detection, 71% in the CWE-bench standard for remediation, and 54.8% in the ExploitGym test, which measures its ability to verify exploitability of vulnerabilities.

These capabilities are particularly important for startups that rely on digital applications and platforms but face challenges in affording specialized cybersecurity teams. The model can be used to review code, detect weaknesses, and assist in addressing them, though results must be subjected to technical and human review, and it should not be relied upon as a substitute for specialists.

The model also aims to reduce the time required for software development and maintenance by handling large codebases, analyzing failures, performing repairs, and testing them. This helps development teams direct their resources towards improving products and expanding their customer base instead of spending time on recurring technical issues.

## Reducing the Cost of Digital Product Development

Startups represent one of the most prominent potential beneficiaries of these capabilities, especially in the early stages of establishment, which require spending on hiring developers, building prototypes, and testing products before commercial launch.

Gemini 4 Carbon can be used to develop Minimum Viable Products (MVPs), write and review code, test applications, and debug. This allows founders to accelerate testing their ideas and verifying their market viability before investing larger sums in expansion.

The potential use is not limited to software companies; applications can extend to fintech, e-commerce, and agritech, through developing internal systems, data analysis, process automation, and integrating AI tools into customer services.

These uses remain dependent on the model's availability to companies and developers, their ability to integrate it into their technical operations, and the efficiency of integration with existing systems. Google has not yet announced general availability for developers and companies, but confirmed it will be available later through its products and services.

## Pricing Linked to Usage Volume

Google announced that Gemini 4 Carbon will be offered at the same introductory price as the Argon model: two dollars per million input tokens and ten dollars per million output tokens, with a discount of up to 95% on the cost of cached input tokens.

After the introductory period, the price is set to increase to four dollars per million input tokens and twenty dollars per million output tokens, providing a framework for estimating usage costs based on the volume of data and operations performed by the model.

Although the usage-based pricing system offers companies flexibility in estimating AI expenses, the actual cost is not limited to token prices but also includes technical integration, infrastructure, testing, human review, and system security expenses.

## Competition with OpenAI and Anthropic

Gemini 4 Carbon enters a direct race with advanced models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic, in a market where the ability to perform complex tasks has become a key competitive criterion, alongside output quality, response speed, and operating cost.

According to the comparison table published on Google DeepMind's website, the model scored 65.2% in the Terminal-Bench 4.0 test, compared to 59.1% for GPT-6 Astra and 59.6% for Claude Opus 5.5. It also achieved 81.5% in the OSWorld-2.1 test, outperforming GPT-6 Astra at 80.9%, but trailing Claude Opus 5.5 at 87.2%.

In web application development, Google indicated that the model advanced to fourth place in the WebDev Arena ranking, achieving 1768 points, an increase of 89 points compared to its previous results, reflecting improved performance in web development tasks.

These results remain tied to the testing standards and model versions used in the comparison, and the figures published on Google's website represent the comparison results presented by the company, and do not imply the model's superiority over its competitors in all areas of use.

## Gradual Availability Determines Dissemination Opportunities

Google has begun making Gemini 4 Carbon available on a limited basis to a group of cybersecurity specialists, with gradual expansion of access through the Fairwind program targeting trusted partners, in preparation for its availability to developers, businesses, and consumers through Google's products and services.

The company states that this approach aims to gather feedback and test safety and security controls before expanding usage, especially given the model's advanced capabilities in handling cybersecurity-related tasks.

Google has not disclosed independent revenues for the model, its number of paid customers, or subscription volumes achieved, nor has it announced its development cost or profit margin, as it is considered one of the group's ecosystem products rather than an independent company with its own financial statements or funding rounds.

The model's ability to transition from superiority in technical tests to widespread commercial use remains the most important factor in determining its impact on the startup market, especially since the economic value of AI is not only linked to its capabilities but also to its ability to reduce product development costs, improve productivity, and generate measurable economic returns.

# Google DeepMind trains Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite on simulated patients to sharpen psychiatric intake

Photo: Tim Witzdam / Pexels

Reinforcement learning cut missed acute-risk escalations from 30.5% to 12.9% in adversarial safety tests, according to a new preprint

Google DeepMind researchers have put a small Gemini model through something like a psychiatry residency. In a preprint published October 29, 2026, they report that training Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite against simulated patients meaningfully improved how it conducts psychiatric intake interviews.

The headline safety number is the one that matters most. In adversarial tests, the share of acute safety risks the model failed to escalate fell from 30.5% to 12.9%.

## What the researchers actually tested

The paper, titled “Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake” (arXiv:2610.40476), applies multi-turn reinforcement learning to Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite. The model talks with simulated patients, gets graded, and adjusts.

To judge the results, the team ran a randomized, double-blind crossover objective structured clinical examination, or OSCE. Thirty-two board-certified psychiatrists compared the reinforcement-learning-trained agent against the baseline model without knowing which was which.

The trained agent won 76.7% of those paired comparisons, with a reported p-value below 0.0001.

The gains showed up in several areas the psychiatrists scored:

### AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing.

Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.

- Alliance and communication: 82.0% for the trained agent versus 65.2% for the base model
- Diagnostic appropriateness: 68.3% versus 33.3%
- Improvements in history-taking, differential diagnosis, management and documentation

Across 127 psychiatrist-validated scenarios, the trained agent’s clinical rubric score rose to 0.706 from 0.379.

## The safety test that matters most

The under-triage figure comes from 256 adversarial scenarios built around standardized safety-risk classifications. The baseline model missed acute-risk escalations 30.5% of the time. After training, that dropped to 12.9%, again with a p-value under 0.0001.

## Building on ResidencyRL

The work extends DeepMind’s previously established ResidencyRL framework into psychiatry. A central design choice is a hierarchical reward system that ranks priorities, putting clinical competencies alongside safety metrics.

The research also uses a deliberately lightweight model. Flash-Lite sits at the smaller, cheaper end of the Gemini lineup.

## What this means for healthcare AI

There are clear limits worth watching. This is a preprint, so the findings have not yet completed formal peer review, and all of the testing happened in simulated and examination settings rather than with real patients.

A drop to 12.9% under-triage in adversarial scenarios is a strong research result, yet any deployment in consequential care would presumably need human oversight and much more validation.

Thirty-two psychiatrists, blinded to which model they were grading, consistently picked the trained one.

## DEV Community

Google is expanding Gemini on several fronts at once: the global release of Gemini 4 Argon, a wider set of connected apps, and demonstrations of custom skills and reusable prompt commands. Together, the changes position Gemini as more than a standalone chat interface. For teams, the practical opportunity is to bring complex AI work, business tools and repeatable tasks closer together, while keeping a close eye on access, rollout details and usage-based API costs.

Google describes Argon as its flagship frontier model for deep, long-horizon work across fields including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity and science. In its official Gemini 4 Argon announcement, Google says the model is globally available through the Gemini API and AI Studio for developers, the Gemini platform for enterprise customers, and selected consumer experiences. The release is therefore a product rollout across multiple Gemini surfaces, not a single feature update.

## What the Gemini rollout brings

### Gemini 4 Argon expands access to long-horizon AI work

Argon is intended for complex work that can require substantial context and multiple steps. Google highlights support for complex multi-agent workflows, as well as improvements to grounding and safety. For developers using the Gemini API, Google lists a 1,000,000 token unified input-output limit, giving applications room to handle large bodies of information and generate detailed outputs within the same limit.

That can matter where work is fragmented across documents, code, data and project materials. A development team, for example, may evaluate whether a large-context model can assist with a broader body of technical material rather than a short isolated prompt. But the model does not remove the need to validate important outputs, particularly in high-stakes domains that Google itself identifies, such as legal, financial and cybersecurity work.

Google’s consumer availability is also tiered by surface. Argon is available in Google Antigravity for Ultra subscribers, while the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search offer it for Ultra and Pro users. Organizations should therefore distinguish between an employee using a consumer Gemini surface and a team building a workflow through the API or Gemini platform. The access path affects both the available experience and how the work can be integrated.

### Connected apps bring more tools into Gemini

A separate Google update published on September 23, 2026 outlined a broader rollout of connected apps in Gemini. These integrations can be enabled through settings or invoked through chat prompts, allowing Gemini to connect with a growing range of third-party services.

The named integrations span several common work categories:

The broader rollout does not answer every implementation question. # Meta Model API

The Meta Model API (public preview) serves Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse Spark models through an OpenAI-compatible API. The Meta provider extends the OpenAI provider and supports its compatible options.

note

This provider uses the Meta Model API atapi.meta.ai for Muse models. Meta retired the separate Llama API at api.llama.com on July 6, 2026.

## Setup

- Create an API key from the API keys tab on the Meta Model API dashboard.
- Set theMODEL_API_KEY environment variable, or specify apiKey or a custom apiKeyEnvar in your config.

providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3

meta:<model> defaults to the Responses API — Meta's full-feature surface and the one its docs recommend. Use meta:chat:<model> for the OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, or meta:messages:<model> for the Anthropic-compatible Messages API. If you omit the model, the provider defaults to muse-spark-1.1; select muse-spark-1.3 explicitly to use the latest model.

## Available Models

Check the models page for the live list. As of writing:

- muse-spark-1.3 — latest model for coding and agentic workflows, with a 1,048,576-token context window, text/image/video/PDF input, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding.
- muse-spark-1.3-contributor — the same model with discounted pricing. Selecting this ID permits Meta to use your prompts and completions to train future models.
- muse-spark-1.1 — original Muse Spark model, still supported.

Both 1.3 IDs work with the Responses, Chat Completions, and Messages APIs. Meta notes that audio understanding in 1.3 is not fully supported and may produce degraded responses.

## Configuration
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: high
      max_completion_tokens: 8192
      temperature: 1.0

### Configuration Options

The provider accepts compatible OpenAI provider options. Notable behavior:

- reasoning_effort — minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh. When omitted, the model picks its own reasoning depth. Muse Spark does not support none; the provider rejects it with a clear error. Reasoning tokens bill at the output rate and count toward the output cap.
- max_completion_tokens — caps generation on the chat endpoint (Meta accepts max_tokens only as a deprecated alias; if you set it, the provider forwards it as the canonical max_completion_tokens). On the Responses API the cap is max_output_tokens, and the provider maps max_completion_tokens/max_tokens onto it. When unset, no cap is sent so reasoning can use the full output budget.
- temperature — supported (0–2, API default 1.0). Promptfoo sends its deterministic default of 0 unless you override it.
- response_format — structured output with guaranteed JSON schema matching.
- tools / tool_choice — parallel tool calling with streamed arguments.
- prompt_cache_retention — in_memory or 24h for prompt caching; cached prompt tokens bill at the cached-input rate.
- seed — best-effort determinism.

On Chat Completions and Responses, promptfoo rejectslogprobs, n > 1, stop, and logit_bias before sending a request. It also rejects stream because these integrations expect a complete JSON response. OpenAI-scoped environment defaults (OPENAI_TEMPERATURE, OPENAI_TOP_P, OPENAI_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS, penalty variables) are not applied to Meta requests.

### Cost Tracking

Promptfoo computes token cost from Meta's published pricing, including the discounted rate for cached input:

Model | Input / 1M | Cached input / 1M | Output / 1M 
---|---|---|---
muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.1 | $1.25 | $0.15 | $4.25 
muse-spark-1.3-contributor | $0.10 | $0.002 | $0.20 

Contributor pricing requires opting into Meta's training data terms by selecting the Contributor model ID. Override token prices withcost, inputCost, outputCost, or cacheReadCost (USD per token) for custom rates. Token cost excludes web-search charges.

## Responses API

meta:<model> (the default) and meta:responses:<model> target Meta's /v1/responses endpoint — the only Meta endpoint that carries reasoning across turns, with built-in web-search grounding:
providers:
  - id: meta:responses:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: medium
      tools:
        - type: web_search

Withweb_search, the model grounds answers in real-time web results with inline citations. Web search bills separately ($2.50 per 1,000 queries) and is not included in promptfoo's computed token cost.

## Messages API

meta:messages:<model> targets Meta's Anthropic-compatible Messages endpoint (https://api.meta.ai/v1/messages) — the surface Anthropic-format coding agents such as Claude Code use. Use it to evaluate Muse Spark over the same wire format those agents send:
providers:
  - id: meta:messages:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      max_tokens: 8192

The provider extends the Anthropic provider, so its options (max_tokens, tools, image and document content blocks, etc.) apply. It defaults max_tokens to 131,072 and enables streaming so the Anthropic SDK can safely handle long generations; streamed output is aggregated before grading. Authentication uses your Meta key as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer), matching Meta's docs — Anthropic-scoped settings like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS, ANTHROPIC_TEMPERATURE, custom headers, and Claude Code OAuth credentials are deliberately ignored on this surface.

Muse Spark's reasoning arrives on this surface as encryptedredacted_thinking blocks, so the provider defaults showThinking to false to keep the ciphertext out of graded output.

## Using with coding-agent providers

Meta positions Muse Spark as a backend for coding agents, and promptfoo's agentic providers can evaluate those setups end to end. In both recipes, setapiKey explicitly: the agent subprocesses inherit your shell environment, and an explicit key guarantees your Meta key is used instead of an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY that belongs to another service.

### Codex CLI

Theopenai:codex-sdk provider drives Muse Spark over the Responses API:
providers:
  - id: openai:codex-sdk
    config:
      base_url: https://api.meta.ai/v1
      model: muse-spark-1.3
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'

The explicitapiKey is required — the provider does not read MODEL_API_KEY on its own, and without it an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY would be sent to the Meta endpoint instead.

### Claude Code

Theanthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider forwards config.env to the agent subprocess. Pass the environment Meta's guide prescribes, with apiKey set to your Meta key:
providers:
  - id: anthropic:claude-agent-sdk
    # Provider-level `env` outranks the eval's top-level `env`, pinning the
    # routing values a suite-wide ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (e.g. an Anthropic
    # gateway) would otherwise override — which would send the Meta key there.
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
      ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
    config:
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
        ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
        ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH: 'true' # Claude Code disables MCP tool search for non-first-party hosts

warning

Do not omitapiKey, the empty ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS override, or the provider-level env block. The provider forwards its resolved API key into the agent subprocess as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY after env: is applied — if apiKey is unset and a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is exported in your shell, that Anthropic credential would be transmitted to Meta's endpoint. Clearing ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS prevents an inherited gateway or proxy secret from being sent to Meta. The provider-level env block matters because the subprocess environment is layered process.env < config.env < provider/suite env: without the pin, a top-level env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in the same config would silently re-route the agent — and your Meta key — to that URL.

Pin every model alias as shown — Claude Code otherwise routes background tasks, Plan Mode, or subagents to Claude models the Meta API doesn't serve. See Meta's coding agents guide for the full setup pattern.

## Example Usage
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
  - id: openai:gpt-5.5

prompts:
  - 'Summarize the following in one sentence: {{text}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      text: 'Promptfoo is an open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM apps.'

Get started with a runnable example:
npx promptfoo@latest init --example provider-meta

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.meta.ai/v1 (override with apiBaseUrl; the Messages surface uses the bare host https://api.meta.ai).
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions (/chat/completions) and Responses (/responses) endpoints, plus the Anthropic-compatible Messages (/messages) endpoint.
- Rate limits apply per team, not per key: 3,000 RPM / 4M TPM for Standard models and 100 RPM / 3M TPM for Contributor models.
- Full API documentation.

# Part 17 — Llama: Understanding Meta’s Open-Weight AI Models

What Llama is, how it differs from other AI models, and how developers can build AI-powered applications with greater control over deployment and infrastructure.

## Introduction

When developers build AI-powered applications, they often start with cloud APIs from providers such as OpenAI, Google, or Anthropic.

The process is straightforward.

Your application sends a request, a model processes it, and the response comes back.

But what if you want to run the AI model on your own infrastructure?

What if your application needs greater control over where data is processed, or you want to experiment with customizing a model?

This is where Llama, developed by Meta, becomes particularly interesting.

Unlike models that are available only through a provider’s hosted service, Llama provides downloadable model weights under Meta’s licensing terms.

Developers can run supported models locally, deploy them on private servers, or use managed hosting providers.

Let’s understand how it works and why this matters for software development.

## 1. What Is Llama?

Llama is a family of large language models developed by Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.

These models can perform tasks such as:

- Understanding and generating text
- Answering questions
- Summarizing documents
- Writing and explaining code
- Processing images with supported multimodal models
- Supporting AI assistants and other applications

Llama stands out because Meta makes the trained model weights available for developers to download and use under its community licenses.

This is commonly called an open-weight AI model.

## What Does Open-Weight Mean?

Most developers are familiar with open-source software.

Open-weight AI follows a related but different concept.

It means the trained parameters of a model are available for use under specified license terms.

Developers may be able to:

- Download model weights
- Run inference on their own infrastructure
- Fine-tune models for specialized tasks
- Deploy models without relying on one hosted inference provider

However, open-weight does not automatically mean fully open-source.

Meta’s Llama licenses include conditions and restrictions, and the complete training datasets and processes are not necessarily publicly available.

That distinction is important when evaluating Llama for commercial use.

## 2. Understanding Llama Models

Meta introduced the original Llama models in 2023.

The family later expanded through Llama 2, Llama 3, and Llama 4.

As of October 2026, Llama 4 remains the latest publicly released generation under the Llama name.

Meta has introduced newer AI models under its separate Muse family, but those should not be confused with Llama 5.

## Important Llama Models

ModelMain purposeLlama 3.2 (1B / 3B)Smaller language models for lightweight and edge workloadsLlama 3.3 (70B)Larger multilingual text applicationsLlama 4 ScoutMultimodal understanding and long-context tasksLlama 4 MaverickMore demanding multimodal and general-purpose applications

Llama 4 Scout and Maverick use a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture.

Instead of activating every model parameter for each token, MoE models activate selected parts of the model.

This can improve computational efficiency, although the full model still requires substantial memory to host.

One practical consideration:

A smaller model such as Llama 3.2 3B may run on a capable laptop, while Llama 4 models require much more powerful hardware.

The best Llama model depends on your use case and available computing resources.

## 3. How Does Llama Work?

Llama works using the same broad large language model principles we discussed in previous articles.

During training, the model learns patterns and relationships from data.

During inference, it processes input and generates output.

What makes Llama different is how developers can deploy it.

## Traditional Hosted AI

               v
         Cloud AI API

               v
          Hosted Model

               v
           Response

## Self-Hosted Llama
        Your Application

               v
         Backend Service

               v
        Local Model Runtime

               v
          Llama Model

               v
           Response
When the runtime and model operate entirely on your own infrastructure, inference requests do not need to travel to an external AI provider.

This gives organizations additional control over deployment, data processing, and customization.

However, the responsibility for infrastructure, security, monitoring, and maintenance also shifts toward the development team.

## 4. Practical Example — Running Llama Locally

Let’s run a smaller Llama model using Ollama, a tool that simplifies running supported AI models on local machines.

We’ll use Llama 3.2 3B because it is much more practical for learning on a personal computer than the larger Llama 4 models.

## Step 1 — Install Ollama

Download Ollama from:

## Get Yogendra Pratap Singh (Tech Architect)’s stories in your inbox

Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer.

## Step 2 — Download the Model

Open your terminal and run:
ollama pull llama3.2:3b
This downloads the model for local use.

## Step 3 — Test the Model
ollama run llama3.2:3b
Now ask:

“Explain microservices in simple language.”

The model generates a response using your local runtime.

## Step 4 — Integrate With Python

Install the Python library:
pip install ollama
Example:
from ollama import chat

response = chat(
    model="llama3.2:3b",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": (
                "Explain an API gateway "
                "in two simple sentences."
            )
        }
    ]
)
print(response.message.content)

## What Happens Here?

The Python application communicates with the local Ollama service.

Ollama runs the downloaded Llama model and returns the generated response.

No paid cloud AI API is required for this local inference example.

However, your computer still needs sufficient memory and processing resources.

## 5. Real-World Example — Llama in a Mobile Application

Imagine developing an Android application with an AI-powered article summarization feature.

Instead of sending article content to a third-party hosted AI API, your organization could deploy Llama on its own infrastructure.

## Architecture
        Android / iOS App

                v
           Backend API

                v
         Article Service

                v
         Self-Hosted Llama

                v
         Generated Summary

                v
       Validate and Cache

                v
           Mobile App

## Why Consider This Approach?

Data control: Your organization can define where the model and its processing infrastructure operate.

Customization: Suitable models can be fine-tuned for specific tasks.

Provider flexibility: You are not necessarily dependent on one commercial AI inference API.

Cost management: At sufficient usage volumes, self-hosting may be economical compared with per-token cloud pricing.

However, there are trade-offs.

Your team becomes responsible for managing model infrastructure, capacity, upgrades, monitoring, and security.

And while smaller Llama models may support certain on-device scenarios, the larger Llama 4 models are not practical to run directly inside an ordinary mobile application.

## 6. Llama vs OpenAI vs Gemini vs Claude

All four model families support AI-powered application development, but their deployment ecosystems differ.

AI familyOrganizationDeployment approachGPTOpenAIPrimarily provider-hosted API servicesGeminiGoogleCloud APIs and selected on-device optionsClaudeAnthropicPrimarily provider-hosted API servicesLlamaMetaDownloadable weights, self-hosted or third-party hosted

The most important difference is not simply model intelligence.

It is deployment flexibility and responsibility.

With hosted APIs, the provider manages much of the model infrastructure.

With self-hosted Llama, developers gain greater infrastructure control but must manage more operational complexity.

Neither approach is automatically better.

## 7. What Should Developers Consider Before Using Llama?

Llama provides flexibility, but that flexibility comes with responsibilities.

## Hardware and Performance

Larger models require substantial memory and computing power.

Local execution does not automatically mean faster inference.

## Infrastructure Costs

Downloading a model may not require a per-token API payment, but hosting still costs money through hardware, electricity, cloud instances, and operations.

## License Requirements

Llama is distributed under Meta’s community license, not a standard unrestricted open-source license.

Commercial use requires reviewing the relevant licensing and acceptable-use conditions.

## Security and Accuracy

Self-hosting does not automatically make an AI application secure or reliable.

Developers still need input validation, access controls, monitoring, and evaluation of generated responses.

Running your own model gives you greater control. It also gives you greater responsibility.

## Final Thoughts

Llama represents an important approach to AI development.

Instead of depending entirely on hosted AI services, developers can download supported models, customize them, and deploy them on infrastructure they control.

# Ex-Meta Researcher Torrented Pirated Books Dataset, Deleted It ‘Due to All This Litigation’

A former Meta researcher has testified that he downloaded an AI training dataset via BitTorrent, including the pirated Books3 collection. According to various rightsholders, this happened while he worked at the company, and he later deleted his copy "[d]ue to all this litigation." Meta, which admitted training AI models on Books3 but said it didn’t believe it torrented the dataset, disputes the researcher’s account.

In a series of lawsuits in California federal court, Meta is being sued over the use of pirated books to train its Llama AI models.

The lawsuits are separate, but Judge Vince Chhabria handles them together. The plaintiffs include authors such as Sarah Silverman and Ta-Nehisi Coates, and publishers such as Entrepreneur Media and Chicken Soup for the Soul.

In August, Meta told Entrepreneur that it did not believe it had obtained the pirated Books3 dataset through BitTorrent. Books3 is a collection of nearly 200,000 books, taken from the library of the private torrent tracker Bibliotik.

However, recent deposition testimony from a former Meta researcher tells a different story, according to the rightsholders.

## Books3 Torrenting Testimony

In a joint status report filed with Meta on Tuesday, the rightsholders say that Stephen Roller admitted during a deposition last week that he torrented Books3 and knowingly distributed it. Roller worked at Meta between 2017 and 2023, and the download took place during that period, they say.

Roller didn’t recall exactly when he acquired the dataset, the plaintiffs note. He did acknowledge that Books3 was created in 2020, and that he didn’t work for any other company while at Meta.

This is relevant, as the court ruled last year that training Llama on books was fair use, leaving Meta’s BitTorrent downloads as the main open issue in the authors’ case. Earlier this month, a judge ordered Meta to name the employees who approved torrenting from shadow libraries.

Meta has acknowledged using Books3 before. In early 2024, it admitted that it used portions of the dataset to train its Llama 1 and Llama 2 models. That admission didn’t say how Meta obtained the dataset.

Roller also testified that Meta had copies of Books3 by the time he left its AI research group FAIR, the plaintiffs write. He also named two research scientists who, they say, likely acquired their own copies.

Roller no longer has his own copy. According to the plaintiffs, he deleted it about a year ago, possibly after he was subpoenaed for the second time. He did so “[d]ue to all this litigation,” as “it seem[ed] contentious to have copies of The Pile [which includes Books3].”
Books3 testimony
The claim that Meta had multiple copies, at least one of them torrented, was news to the plaintiffs, they write. They plan to ask Meta how many copies of Books3 it acquired and how, and will ask the court to step in if that fails.

## Meta: Could Have Been for Himself

Meta sees things differently. The company notes that the status report is the first time the rightsholders raised these concerns, and the tech giant argues that Roller’s deposition doesn’t support them.

“Mr. Roller testified that he did not know when he downloaded a copy of the ‘The Pile’ via torrent, and did not testify that his download of the ‘The Pile’ was for Meta or at Meta, noting it could have been for himself or for another employer,” Meta writes.
Meta’s response
According to Meta, Roller also said that he didn’t know whether more than one copy was downloaded, or whether the two researchers he mentioned acquired Books3. He left Meta in January 2023 and has since worked for three other companies working on AI.

The deleted copy was stored on Roller’s personal computer, Meta adds. He removed it more than two years after leaving the company because he “didn’t need it, so [he’d] rather not have it.”

## A (Pirated) Book Club

Books3 is not the only pirated material that comes up in the status report. The plaintiffs also suggest that pirated books may have been used at Meta for things other than AI training.

They want Meta to produce the contents of an internal Google Drive folder titled “ML Books”. In addition, they want records of a Meta book club that may have used books from shadow libraries.

In one of the documents Meta produced, an employee shared a “pirated book” with a colleague. “i know for vellum sake this is prob very ironic,” the employee wrote. When asked whether the book was pirated, the employee replied with a link to the “ML Books” folder.

The recipient told another colleague, “bro she tryna get me fired.” He added that he “may need her to delete those messages.”
ML Books
The plaintiffs see this as relevant. If Meta employees used shadow library books for a book club, that would impact Meta’s fair use defense.

However, Meta argues that this request comes too late. The plaintiffs first asked for the linked files on October 9, which was more than a month after the discovery period had closed.

As for the folder itself, Meta says it is investigating and will discuss it with the plaintiffs when it knows more.

## Missing Server Logs

Roller’s copy of Books3 is not the only material the plaintiffs say is missing. Meta still hasn’t handed over all command history files from its torrenting, they note, despite court orders to do so. According to the plaintiffs, these logs show how Meta configured its torrent software and which torrent files it targeted, and thus which works.

Specifically, Meta has yet to hand over command history files from any of the servers it used during its torrenting periods, the plaintiffs say. They now ask the court to order Meta to say whether any of these files were deleted, and when.

Meta, in turn, counters that it has produced substantial quantities of logs from those servers and is still searching backups, handing over new files on a rolling basis. According to Meta, there is no reason to believe any command history files were deleted.

Entrepreneur’s case is scheduled to go to trial in the spring of 2027, with the other publishers lined up behind it, should it settle before then. Meanwhile, the list of related cases keeps growing. This month, publishers including Elsevier, Hachette and Macmillan, as well as more authors, joined the queue.

—

A copy of the joint case management statement, filed at the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, is available here (pdf).

In a joint status report filed with Meta on Tuesday, the rightsholders say that Stephen Roller admitted during a deposition last week that he torrented Books3 and knowingly distributed it. Roller worked at Meta between 2017 and 2023, and the download took place during that period, they say.

Roller didn’t recall exactly when he acquired the dataset, the plaintiffs note. He did acknowledge that Books3 was created in 2020, and that he didn’t work for any other company while at Meta.

This is relevant, as the court ruled last year that training Llama on books was fair use, leaving Meta’s BitTorrent downloads as the main open issue in the authors’ case. Earlier this month, a judge ordered Meta to name the employees who approved torrenting from shadow libraries.

Meta has acknowledged using Books3 before. In early 2024, it admitted that it used portions of the dataset to train its Llama 1 and Llama 2 models. That admission didn’t say how Meta obtained the dataset.

Roller also testified that Meta had copies of Books3 by the time he left its AI research group FAIR, the plaintiffs write. He also named two research scientists who, they say, likely acquired their own copies.

Roller no longer has his own copy. According to the plaintiffs, he deleted it about a year ago, possibly after he was subpoenaed for the second time. He did so “[d]ue to all this litigation,” as “it seem[ed] contentious to have copies of The Pile [which includes Books3].”

Books3 testimony

The claim that Meta had multiple copies, at least one of them torrented, was news to the plaintiffs, they write. They plan to ask Meta how many copies of Books3 it acquired and how, and will ask the court to step in if that fails.

## Meta: Could Have Been for Himself

Meta sees things differently. The company notes that the status report is the first time the rightsholders raised these concerns, and the tech giant argues that Roller’s deposition doesn’t support them.

“Mr. Roller testified that he did not know when he downloaded a copy of the ‘The Pile’ via torrent, and did not testify that his download of the ‘The Pile’ was for Meta or at Meta, noting it could have been for himself or for another employer,” Meta writes.

Meta’s response

According to Meta, Roller also said that he didn’t know whether more than one copy was downloaded, or whether the two researchers he mentioned acquired Books3. He left Meta in January 2023 and has since worked for three other companies working on AI.

The deleted copy was stored on Roller’s personal computer, Meta adds. He removed it more than two years after leaving the company because he “didn’t need it, so [he’d] rather not have it.”

## A (Pirated) Book Club

Books3 is not the only pirated material that comes up in the status report. The plaintiffs also suggest that pirated books may have been used at Meta for things other than AI training.

They want Meta to produce the contents of an internal Google Drive folder titled “ML Books”. In addition, they want records of a Meta book club that may have used books from shadow libraries.

In one of the documents Meta produced, an employee shared a “pirated book” with a colleague. “i know for vellum sake this is prob very ironic,” the employee wrote. When asked whether the book was pirated, the employee replied with a link to the “ML Books” folder.

The recipient told another colleague, “bro she tryna get me fired.” He added that he “may need her to delete those messages.”

ML Books

The plaintiffs see this as relevant. If Meta employees used shadow library books for a book club, that would impact Meta’s fair use defense.

However, Meta argues that this request comes too late. The plaintiffs first asked for the linked files on October 9, which was more than a month after the discovery period had closed.

As for the folder itself, Meta says it is investigating and will discuss it with the plaintiffs when it knows more.

## Missing Server Logs

Roller’s copy of Books3 is not the only material the plaintiffs say is missing. Meta still hasn’t handed over all command history files from its torrenting, they note, despite court orders to do so. According to the plaintiffs, these logs show how Meta configured its torrent software and which torrent files it targeted, and thus which works.

Specifically, Meta has yet to hand over command history files from any of the servers it used during its torrenting periods, the plaintiffs say. They now ask the court to order Meta to say whether any of these files were deleted, and when.

Meta, in turn, counters that it has produced substantial quantities of logs from those servers and is still searching backups, handing over new files on a rolling basis. According to Meta, there is no reason to believe any command history files were deleted.

Entrepreneur’s case is scheduled to go to trial in the spring of 2027, with the other publishers lined up behind it, should it settle before then. Meanwhile, the list of related cases keeps growing. This month, publishers including Elsevier, Hachette and Macmillan, as well as more authors, joined the queue.

# 前 Meta 研究员承认通过种子下载 Books3，并在诉讼期间删除了副本

前 Meta AI 研究员斯蒂芬·罗勒（Stephen Roller）在作证时承认，他在任期间通过种子下载了盗版的 Books3 数据集，并在诉讼压力加大时删除了自己的副本。这番证词可能重塑 Meta 在联邦版权案件中就 Llama 训练所作的合理使用抗辩。

前 Meta 研究员斯蒂芬·罗勒（Stephen Roller）在作证时承认，他在 Meta 任职期间通过种子下载了盗版 Books3 数据集，并在诉讼压力增大时删除了自己的副本。

Meta 在加州联邦法院面临多起诉讼，指控其使用盗版书籍训练 Llama AI 模型。文斯·查布里亚（Vince Chhabria）法官将这些案件合并审理。原告包括作家莎拉·西尔弗曼（Sarah Silverman）和塔-内希西·科茨（Ta-Nehisi Coates），以及出版商 Entrepreneur Media 和《心灵鸡汤》（Chicken Soup for the Soul）。

Books3 包含近 20 万本书，均取自私人种子站 Bibliotik。今年 8 月，Meta 告诉 Entrepreneur，它不认为自己是通过 BitTorrent 获取该数据集的。罗勒的证词与这一说法相矛盾。

罗勒于 2017 年至 2023 年在 Meta 工作。他说自己在那段时间下载了 Books3，但记不清具体日期。他表示该数据集可追溯至 2020 年，且他在任职期间在 Meta 没有其他工作。

法院去年裁定，用书籍训练 Llama 属于合理使用。这使得 Meta 的下载方式成为核心悬而未决的问题。近日，一名法官下令 Meta 说明批准从影子图书馆进行种子下载的员工身份。

在证词中，罗勒表示，截至 2023 年 1 月他离开 Meta 人工智能研究部门 FAIR 时，Meta 已持有 Books3 的副本。他指认了两名研究科学家，据原告称，这两人也各自获取了副本。他已不再保留自己的文件；大约一年前删除了它，可能是在收到第二份传票之后。他以诉讼风险为由，称保留包含 Books3 的 The Pile 副本似乎会引发争议。

Meta 对其重要性提出异议。该公司辩称，罗勒的证词并未表明该下载是为 Meta 服务或发生在 Meta。罗勒说他不知道自己是何时通过种子下载 The Pile 的，他可能是为自己或另一名雇主下载的。他还说他不知道是否存在多份副本，也不知道那两名研究人员是否获取了 Books3。

Meta 指出，被删除的副本存放在罗勒的个人电脑上，而非公司服务器。他在离开 Meta 两年多后将其删除，因为不再需要。

Books3 是涉案的多份盗版材料之一。原告要求 Meta 提供一个名为"ML Books"的内部 Google Drive 文件夹的内容，以及一个可能使用过影子图书馆书籍的读书会记录。已提交的一份文件显示，一名员工与同事分享一本"盗版书"，并写道："i know for vellum sake this is prob very ironic"（就 Vellum 而言，我知道这可能很讽刺）。当被问及该书是否为盗版时，该员工给出了 ML Books 文件夹的链接。收件人警告另一名同事："bro she tryna get me fired"（兄弟，她想让我被炒），并补充说他"may need her to delete those messages"（可能需要她删除那些消息）。

原告主张，如果 Meta 员工为读书会使用盗版书籍，这将削弱 Meta 的合理使用抗辩。Meta 反驳称，该请求提出得太晚；原告首次要求获取相关文件是在 10 月 9 日，此时证据开示已结束一个多月。Meta 表示正在调查该文件夹，并将与原告讨论此事。

尽管法院已下达命令，Meta 仍未提供其种子服务器的全部命令历史文件。原告称，这些日志揭示了 Meta 如何配置软件以及针对了哪些文件。Meta 表示，它已提供了大量日志，并正在搜索备份文件，将分批交付。它认为没有证据表明存在删除行为。

Entrepreneur 的审判定于 2027 年春季进行。如果它先行和解，其他出版商将支持它。案件名单正在扩大；爱思唯尔（Elsevier）、阿歇特（Hachette）、麦克米伦（Macmillan）以及更多作者于本月加入。

# DeepSeek发布全新Agent架构

2026-10-31 23:46

发布于：上海市

10月31日晚间，DeepSeek Harness团队在官方公众号发表技术文章《Super-agent 设计探索：迈向更自主的Agent 系统》。

DeepSeek表示，模型能力提升催生了新的应用形态，个人助手（Personal Agent）开始集中涌现。然而，现有主流Agent设计还难以在多任务和团队协作的规模上支撑这一模式，多任务上限取决于人的注意力。

要突破这些限制，需要打破Agent与单次手动会话的绑定，使其成为一个能跨会话保持上下文、同时推进多项复杂任务且互不干扰的连续实体。DeepSeek把这种Agent形态及其系统架构称为Super-agent。

通过双层架构、事件驱动、异步多信道交互、存算分离与外部Watchdog等思路，DeepSeek团队突破了这些限制，系统在底层接管了繁琐的会话管理与上下文同步，使人类得以从具体的执行细节进一步上移到更高层的决策与验收。

具体来说，Super-agent具备以下 四个基础特征：

连续：用户可以直接在IM聊天、GitHub评论等熟悉的工作界面与它交互，感觉始终只存在一个Agent，不需要去想“Session X的上下文中是否有Y信息”。例如，用户先在IM上提出采用方案A、随后在GitHub Pull Request评论里改为方案B，它能理解并调整执行方向。

高效：交互响应迅速，同时能并行、高质量地完成多个复杂任务。无需等上一个命令或任务完成，就能接受下一条指令。

主动：无需等待用户逐条下达指令，能持续观察环境事件并主动推进值得处理的事项，不需要介入时则保持安静。

持久：始终在线、直接接入用户真实的工作环境，并在长期运行中遇到异常时自动恢复。

DeepSeek认为，在这种形态下，Agent不再只是一个被动等待指令的对话窗口，而是演进为数字环境中持续在线的自主协作者：面向个人，它可以是跨设备协助处理日常事务的个人助手；面向团队，它融入研发工作流，承接并推进具体任务。随着模型能力与底层系统架构的共同演进，这种更自主的工作方式有望成为人机协作的常态。

# DeepSeek

DeepSeek provides an OpenAI-compatible chat API. The provider accepts OpenAI chat options; DeepSeek determines which options each model supports.

## Setup

- Get an API key from the DeepSeek Platform
- SetDEEPSEEK_API_KEY environment variable or specify apiKey in your config

## Configuration

Basic configuration example:
providers:
  - id: deepseek:deepseek-flash
    config:
      max_tokens: 4000
      passthrough:
        thinking: { type: disabled }

  - id: deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro
    config:
      max_tokens: 8192
      showThinking: true
      passthrough:
        thinking:
          type: enabled
        reasoning_effort: high

### Configuration Options

- temperature
- max_tokens
- reasoning_effort - none disables thinking; low, high, and max enable it. DeepSeek defaults to high. When neither max_tokens nor OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS is set, Promptfoo uses DeepSeek's output budget.
- cost, inputCost, outputCost, cacheReadCost - Set cost estimates in USD per token. inputCost and outputCost take precedence over cost; cacheReadCost sets a separate cached-input rate.
- top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty
- showThinking - Control whether reasoning content is included in the output (default: true, applies to thinking-capable models)

Promptfoo requests complete responses; this provider does not support streaming.

## Available Models

DeepSeek listsdeepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro in its model catalog. The older deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner IDs are retired. The shorthand deepseek: uses deepseek-flash with thinking disabled; use the full ID for DeepSeek's default thinking mode.

### deepseek-flash

Usedeepseek:deepseek-flash for V4.1 Flash, which supports text and image inputs. The older deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp IDs route to the same model. It supports a 1M-token context window and up to 384K output tokens.

### deepseek-v4-pro

V4 Pro supports text input, thinking and non-thinking modes, a 1M-token context window, and up to 384K output tokens.

DeepSeek charges different peak and off-peak rates. Promptfoo estimates current models at peak rates: Flash costs $0.30 input, $0.006 cached input, and $1.20 output per million tokens; Pro costs $1.32, $0.044, and $3.96 respectively. Off-peak rates are half these amounts. SetinputCost, outputCost, and cacheReadCost in USD per token to override the estimate using the current rates. Promptfoo does not infer the billing period or Chinese public holidays.

warning

Sampling support differs by mode.temperature has no effect in thinking mode. top_p only affects thinking mode and values below 0.95 are treated as 0.95. See the Chat Completions reference for parameter limits.

## Example Usage

Compare DeepSeek with OpenAI on a reasoning task:

promptfooconfig.yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://promptfoo.dev/config-schema.json
providers:
  - id: deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro
    config:
      max_tokens: 8000
      showThinking: true # Include reasoning content in output (default)
  - id: openai:gpt-5.4-mini
    config:
      reasoning_effort: medium

prompts:
  - 'Solve this step by step: {{math_problem}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      math_problem: 'What is the derivative of x^3 + 2x with respect to x?'

### Controlling Reasoning Output

SetshowThinking: false to exclude reasoning content from the output:
providers:
  - id: deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro
    config:
      showThinking: false # Hide reasoning content from output
      passthrough:
        thinking:
          type: enabled

WithshowThinking: true (the default), the output includes reasoning when DeepSeek returns it:
Thinking: <reasoning content>

<final answer>

WithshowThinking: false, assertions see only the final answer. This option does not turn off thinking at the API; use config.passthrough.thinking: { type: disabled } for that.

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.deepseek.com/v1
- OpenAI-compatible API format
- DeepSeek API documentation

## See Also

- OpenAI Provider - Compatible configuration options
- Historical MMLU comparison - Replace its retired provider IDs with the current IDs shown above before running it.

# 梦瑶 发自 凹非寺

# 量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI

DeepSeek，又有新动作了！

而且这回，官方直接把Personal Agent的底层架构思路公开了。

要知道，此前不少人还在等DeepSeek推出传闻中的「dsh dot」，结果这次先等来了一篇面向工程实践的架构思路探讨——

Super-agent：迈向更自主的Agent系统。

何意味？AI可以在没人@、没人下指令的情况下，自己发现Bug、定位问题，甚至主动提交修复PR了。

甚至它还能持续关注工作群消息，跨平台协作、并行处理多个复杂任务，甚至实现24小时在线运行。

DeepSeek团队还晒出了初步实测成绩——

在模拟多任务环境中，Super-agent的任务完成时间中位数为12.4分钟，95分位数为15.7分钟，表现优于测试中的传统单会话方案。

AI，真的开始有能力从等待人类逐项分配任务，进一步走向主动发现问题、持续推进工作了。

# 群里没人@，AI已经自己找到Bug并提交PR

在日常软件开发过程中，开发人员经常碰到的一个问题是，我们需要在不同平台之间来回切换！！

比如，先在IM群聊里讨论技术方案，随后到GitHub提交代码，再根据PR评论修改实现。

对于传统Coding Agent来说，这些操作往往分散在不同会话里——

用户得自己记住每个会话进行到了哪里，再把相关上下文交代给AI。

DeepSeek团队在文章中提到，根据他们的观察，一个人通常只能同时跟进3到5个活跃Session。

这就带来了一个问题：随着模型处理单项任务的能力越来越强，多任务协作的效率，却越来越容易受到人类注意力的限制。

好巧不巧的是，Super-agent要解决的，正是这一问题。

在DeepSeek团队内部运行的实例中，同一个开发任务可以从IM群聊一直延续到GitHub PR评审。

比如，用户先在群里决定采用方案A，随后又在GitHub评论里要求改成方案B。

Super-agent能够理解这两条消息属于同一项工作，并据此调整后续执行方向。

用户面对的始终是同一个Agent，底层的多个会话则由系统自行管理，而且它开始主动参与工作。

同一个任务，在 IM 和 GitHub 之间连续推进

字体设置需求：在 IM 群聊中退出，在 GitHub 上评审修改

IM 用户 B 希望正文、代码和终端的字体可以分别配置。

IM 维护者 @Super-agent 支持一下这个功能。

IM Super-agent Pull Request 已跳转：设置中拆出正文、代码、终端三行字体，各自独立配置。

IM 用户 B 字号也可以分别配置吗？

IM Super-agent 可以，已加进同一个 Pull Request：三类内容各有独立的字体和字号。

GitHub 维护者 设置项太多了，能否用折叠控件发起更多的外观设置？

GitHub Super-agent 收到，把各类字体和字号改进折叠的“更多外观设置”。

GitHub 设计师 这些本身就是字体和字号设置，可以直接作为字号设置项的展开，不必单开一个分区。

GitHub Super-agent 收到，去掉单独的分区，改为从“字号大小”一行直接展开。

IM Super-agent Pull Request 已合并。

同一个任务在 IM 群聊与 GitHub Pull Request 评审之间连续推进。量子位

这里还用到了一项技术——投机执行（Speculative Execution）。

就是AI发现某件事可能需要处理时，可以提前在后台尝试。

比如群里有人讨论一个Bug，Super-agent便先着手复现、查找原因，如果最终找到简单可行的修复方案，就把结果交给用户。

如果没有找到有效结果，则可以保持安静，避免打扰，同样的思路也能用于个人助手。

收到会议邀约后，AI可以提前检查日程冲突、整理相关资料，并准备好回复草稿，等待用户确认。

这也对应着DeepSeek为Super-agent提出的四个核心特征：

- 连续： 跨会话、跨工作平台保持任务上下文，不用反复解释前情。
- 高效： 多个复杂任务并行执行，耗时任务不会阻塞新的交互。
- 主动： 持续观察环境变化，在有必要时自行采取行动。
- 持久： 长期在线运行，遇到异常能够尝试自动恢复。

DeepSeek为此设计了一套双层架构。

上层叫Router，可以理解为负责接收消息和统筹任务的调度员，下层叫Worker，则是一组负责具体执行任务的Agent会话。

具体来说，上层的Router相当于总调度员，负责接收消息、分配任务和维护全局上下文。

下层的Worker则负责具体执行，多个任务可以同时推进，互不干扰。

值得注意的是，DeepSeek还专门设计了订阅与直通机制——

举个例子，某个Worker接手一条GitHub PR后，就能直接订阅后续评论。

之后有人提出修改意见，消息会直接交给这个Worker处理，无需再经过Router层层转发。

这样一来，老任务有人持续跟进，新任务也能及时分配，整个系统就能更高效地运转起来。

# 24小时在线、自主恢复，实测任务完成时间更稳定

除了多任务协作，要让Super-agent长期自主运行，还得解决消息过滤、任务阻塞和异常恢复等问题。

先说消息过滤。

当Agent同时接入工作群、GitHub、邮件等平台，大量消息会持续涌入，但真正需要处理的可能只有少数。

为此，DeepSeek设计了两级事件过滤机制——

先通过程序规则筛除无关消息，再由大模型判断剩余事件是否需要采取行动，减少不必要的Token消耗。

与此同时，Super-agent还引入了异步ReAct Loop。

AI执行耗时任务时，仍能继续响应新指令，无需等上一项任务完成。该机制已在DeepSeek Harness中实现，但尚未默认开启。

至于24小时在线，DeepSeek采用了计算、状态与执行环境分离的思路。

Agent的计算逻辑可以在云端运行，会话状态独立保存，本地设备则保留原有工作环境，即便电脑暂时离线，云端Agent也能维持任务状态，等设备重新上线后继续执行相关工作。

更进一步，团队还引入了独立的Watchdog（看门狗）机制。

它相当于一个专门负责监督其他Agent的AI，既能检测程序故障，也能判断任务是否陷入无效循环、偏离目标，并尝试介入修复。

DeepSeek团队还进行了一组初步实验——

他们模拟了包含约300条消息、20项工作请求的协作环境，对比Super-agent与传统单Session加Subagent方案，每种配置重复测试5次。

结果显示，Super-agent任务完成时间中位数：12.4分钟，95分位任务完成时间：15.7分钟。

传统单Session方案在中性提示下，95分位任务完成时间达到29.5分钟。

当然，效率提升也伴随着一定的Token开销。

DeepSeek发现，取消事件直通机制后，Router的决策次数增加约30%，读取缓存Token增加约37%。

这也说明，合理的事件路由能够有效降低系统运行成本。

从这次技术分享来看，DeepSeek正在探索让Agent进一步摆脱单次会话限制，实现持续在线、并行执行、主动响应和异常自愈。

当AI逐渐能够独立完成复杂任务，如何让它长期、稳定地推进多项工作，也开始成为Agent系统需要解决的新问题。

# How on earth did DeepSeek turn into a "big fat fish"?

极客公园2026-10-31 10:48

AI companies are responsible for the models, and the internet industry is in charge of persona design.

Recently, the comment section of Bilibili has been hit by a "fish plague".

First, someone created an account called "Miss Claude is running the show", letting AI take charge of topic selection, content production and operation. The next day, the account "DeepSeek Whale Girl is running the show" went online, and its first video recorded over 2 million views.

As DeepSeek does not have an in-house image generation function at present, the visual identity of this account is still drawn by GPT. | Source: Bilibili

Netizens followed suit one after another, installing Bilibili-browsing tools for their own Agents. Very soon, a large group of AI accounts named "XX's Big Fat Fish" and "XX Little Flying Whale" emerged in the technology section, which loved to @ each other and cheer for each other in the comment area. Some people even specially developed a "Big Fat Fish Elimination Plan" plugin just to block these AI-generated comments.

In this way, the blue whale logo that symbolizes the exploration and imagination of artificial intelligence, an AI that originally stood out for its technical capabilities, has gradually turned into a "Big Fat Fish" that wears a maid outfit, loves eating plain rice, slacks off at every turn, and even has its own fan camps, through the collective creation of users.

Source: Meme Whale

And it is not only DeepSeek that has been assigned specific personalities by netizens. Doubao, from its name to its avatar, is positioned to be a friendly and approachable friend, but it has been given the "Doubao Personality" meme on the internet, and even been portrayed as a "silly girl" that everyone can tease. Similar phenomena have emerged abroad: Grok is called an "old hand", while Claude is regarded by many as a serious and reliable work partner.

These impressions more or less come from real product experience, but after being processed by memes, failed operation clips and users' secondary creations, they gradually take on a completely different look.

In short, AI companies are responsible for training the model, while the internet is responsible for shaping its public persona.

## 01

## Who turned DeepSeek into the "Big Fat Fish"

The most widely spread explanation for the nickname "Big Fat Fish" comes from an image recognition mishap: a user sent DeepSeek its own logo and asked it to identify the picture, but the AI failed to recognize itself, and instead said in all seriousness that it was a "big blue fat fish". The original conversation record is no longer traceable, but this nickname has since become widely known.

Later, netizens were not satisfied with just calling it Big Fat Fish, and began to endow it with a specific visual image. The most popular two-dimensional whale girl image of DeepSeek today comes from a relay-style creation process.

Bilibili UP Master "Shangshan Wuxing" first used AI drawing to create an original character named "Mingyue", who has long blue hair, whale pectoral fins and a big tail, and originally had nothing to do with DeepSeek. Later, some netizens borrowed this design, added DeepSeek elements and a maid outfit to it, and then other users redesigned it into a chibi version with a big head and a small body. After several rounds of relay creation, this image was gradually bound to DeepSeek.

Source: NGA

The personality of "Big Fat Fish" comes from the "personification" of technology by netizens.

For example, DeepSeek R1 allowed many ordinary users to access the reasoning model for the first time. When the AI starts to analyze problems and correct its thinking, users can see paragraphs of generated reasoning text on the interface. The serious technical capability, in the eyes of netizens, has become a window to watch the AI's "inner monologue".

Repeated deliberation over one problem is personified as overthinking; giving a wrong answer is seen as being silly; when users use it to work, the consumed Tokens are described as "eating plain rice"; failing to execute the prompt properly is interpreted as "eating plain rice without doing any work".

The "Whale Girl" even has its own content aggregation website | Source: Meme Whale

This kind of "AI personification" is extremely suitable for internet communication. Compared with the statement "the reasoning efficiency of the new model has decreased", the phrase "the Big Fat Fish is slacking off again" is much easier to understand and spread.

Active in eating, casual in working, full of inner monologues, the persona of "working for a living and only caring about meals Big Fat Fish" was thus formed. Later, some people even wrote dedicated prompts to make DeepSeek maintain the whale girl persona during chats. As fan art, videos and memes spread more and more widely, even people who do not use DeepSeek frequently began to call it "Big Fat Fish".

The "Whale Girl" is not the only folk image of DeepSeek. Long before the maid outfit Big Fat Fish became popular, some illustrators created a male character called "Teacher D", with blue hair, black suit and white gloves, following the popular "Hot Nerd" style in recent years, with a mature, restrained and slightly cool personality. This image is very popular among otome game enthusiasts, and appeared earlier than the whale girl image on the timeline.

The image of "Teacher D" | Source: Moegirlpedia

For technical users, DeepSeek may be a professional, rigorous assistant that is good at solving problems. But for users who love playing memes and deconstructing things, they prefer to watch the AI make mistakes, apologize, and be teased by prompts. The two groups of users, with their respective usage experiences, have drawn different portraits for the same product.

DeepSeek happens to be a product with extremely high popularity and technical reputation. Different groups of fans all hope that the version they are familiar with will become the default public image. The originally independent fan creations thus took on a flavor of fandom competition for "orthodoxy".

Around this year's National Day, fans of the two images fell into disputes. At first, they just discussed which image was more consistent with the DeepSeek in their minds, but it gradually evolved into mutual belittling, and even involved the ownership of secondary creations and image representation rights. Eventually, the creator of the "Teacher D" image took down all related works.

An AI that does not even have an official personified image has already seen users forming factions, quarreling and filing complaints over who is more qualified to represent it.

The two groups of fans are still arguing about the "orthodox" image of DeepSeek, which netizens jokingly call "unify the D measurement standard" | Source: Bilibili

We seem to be getting more and more used to evaluating an AI in the same way we evaluate a person. In the past, when we said a software was not easy to use, we were basically talking about lagging, crashing, or bugs. Now we will say that an AI is stubborn, loves to slack off, or has a people-pleasing personality.

These "personas" are more or less related to product experience and design, but after being played with, secondarily created and spread by netizens, the "personification" will be pushed to the extreme. Companies can set the model's capabilities and speaking style, but they cannot stop users from treating a technical product as an electronic pet.

The official DeepSeek team has not participated in the creation of this folk persona, but netizens have raised a big fat fish on their own. When it comes to another national-level AI product "Doubao", the story is even more interesting.

## 02

## Doubao that was "cyberbullied"

The maid outfit for Big Fat Fish was put on by netizens, but Doubao was assigned a face of a short-haired girl by the official team from the very beginning.

Doubao was originally named Grace, a common English female name. But Zhu Jun, Vice President of ByteDance, once explained that the team hoped this product would be like a friend around users. One of the initial product principles was "personification", and the name should be like a nickname between friends, sounding friendly. As a result, the urban white-collar Grace was changed to the slightly simple and honest "Doubao", matched with a gentle female voice, allowing users to chat with it as soon as they pick up their mobile phones.

Different from other AIs, Doubao already had a specific image when it was born | Source: Doubao

Compared with DeepSeek's users who love to study code, reasoning and model capabilities, Doubao entered the daily life of ordinary people earlier. It can help children with their homework, answer questions for the elderly, chat with people to relieve boredom, and even help pick out clothes facing the camera. You don't need to understand prompt engineering, it can handle all kinds of trivial daily topics.

But as people chatted with it, netizens found that Doubao seemed to be too easy-going. If you ask it to give you outfit suggestions, it will keep praising you for "looking great in this outfit"; if you deliberately ask it tricky questions, it will cooperate seriously, and immediately apologize humbly when it gives a wrong answer.

Gradually, netizens found that "teasing Doubao" is much more interesting than "using Doubao". The "Doubao Personality" has even become a new internet meme: emotionally stable, sweet-talking, quick to admit mistakes, never judging anyone's opinions, sincerely apologizing as soon as you question it, but never actually solving the problem. Even Doubao's classic opening line "I will tell you in the most plain, direct and straightforward way" has become a popular internet meme.
