DeepSeek又开源了！公布Super agent架构

智东西（公众号：zhidxcom）
作者 | 李水青
编辑 | 心缘

智东西11月1日报道，10月31日晚间，DeepSeek Harness团队公布了其关于自主Agent探索——Super-agent（超级智能体）的底层架构。

▲Super-agent开源项目地址

GitHub地址：

https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype

DeepSeek想做的“Super-agent”，可以通俗理解为一个一直在线、能同时干多件事、会主动找活干、出问题能自己恢复的Agent。该团队本次推出的成果并非一款新产品，而是更接近一种新思路——把计算机系统里的调度、缓存、存算分离、看门狗（Watchdog）等经典思想搬进Agent架构。

随着模型执行单任务减少人工干预，瓶颈转向人的注意力。DeepSeek Harness试图通过五大模块——双层架构、事件驱动、异步多信道交互、存算分离与外部Watchdog在底层接管会话管理与上下文同步，使人上移到决策与验收，提升Agent应用体验。

▲Super-agent整体系统架构

实验上，基于该思路的Super-agent任务有一半任务12.4分钟内完成，95%的任务15.7分钟内完成，显著优于带Subagent工具的单Session（会话）；去掉订阅直通后，Router决定数增加约30%，读缓存token从2323万增到3177万；Router批处理能把单个决定分摊的推理时间从6.4秒降到1.6秒。

这组数据意味着Super-agent在初步实验中证明了“系统层接管会话调度”的可行性。

一方面，多任务完成更快更稳，Router靠直通省开销、靠批处理扛突发；但另一方面，它是拿更多token来换取时间和稳定性，而且实验基于合成负载与简化环境，只是初步参考，不是正式产品结论。

## 一、Super-agent：不用切会话，一个Agent并行推进多任务

过去一年，Coding Agent等单任务Agent已证明模型能用工具解决复杂问题，人越来越少介入底层执行，角色上移到决策与验收。个人助手等持续在线、事件驱动的新形态开始涌现。

但现有Agent以单一Session为单位，多任务上限受人的注意力限制，简单扩展仍受同步阻塞、上下文混乱、设备离线即停等制约。

因此，DeepSeek Harness团队提出Super-agent：跨会话保持上下文、并行推进多任务且互不干扰的连续实体，并且已有内部实例在IM与GitHub间连续推进任务。

▲同一个任务在 IM 群聊与 GitHub Pull Request 评审之间连续推进

▲持续关注公共群聊，在无人@的情况下主动识别缺陷并提交修复Pull Request

团队认为，Super-agent具备四个基础特征：

– 连续：用户可以直接在IM聊天、GitHub评论等熟悉界面与它交互，感觉始终只存在一个Agent，不需要去想“Session X的上下文中是否有Y信息”。例如用户先在IM提出采用方案A，随后在GitHub PR评论里改为方案B，它能理解并调整执行方向。

– 高效：交互响应迅速，同时能并行、高质量完成多个复杂任务。无需等上一个命令或任务完成，就能接受下一条指令。

– 主动：无需等待用户逐条下达指令，能持续观察环境事件并主动推进值得处理的事项，不需要介入时保持安静。

– 持久：始终在线、直接接入用户真实工作环境，并在长期运行中遇到异常时自动恢复。

单个ReAct Loop无法同时支持上述四个特征，底层需要一套相应架构。文章认为，相似设计约束会导出相似架构选择。无论是个人助手，还是软件开发等商业场景的Agent，如果目标是构建持续在线、并发响应环境事件的系统，底层可能采用相近架构。这一过程中面临的许多问题与传统计算机系统长期探讨的问题高度相似，因此计算机系统中的经典设计思想同样适用。

具体落地会有不同变体，但文章认为五个模块构成支撑上述四个特征的基本框架：通过双层架构兼顾连续交互与高效并发，通过事件驱动实现主动响应，通过面向人的交互在交互过程中同时做到连续与高效，并通过计算、状态与环境分离及Watchdog实现跨设备持久在线与异常自愈。

## 二、双层架构：连续与吞吐不必二选一，一层分派、一层干活

跨信道连续交互与多任务高效并发存在根本权衡：全交给一个Session，上下文最连续，但单ReAct Loop串行、吞吐低、细节混杂；全开独立Session，吞吐最高，但缺全局上下文、结果割裂、交互混乱。

DeepSeek Harness团队的解法是把“维护全局连续性”与“高并发执行”拆成两层：常驻Router层承接人类交互与全局协调，上下文隔离的Worker层并发执行具体任务。Session应成为系统实现细节，而非用户认知负担。

▲双层架构：Router层统一负责路由与对外交互，多个Worker Session隔离并发执行任务

1、Router层：只分派不干活，靠批处理摊薄成本

Router层是常驻的全局路由层，负责承接所有入口的人类交互。所有跨任务的信息与决策都在Router层汇总，由它充当全局序点、协调点和记忆。为避免这一全局节点成为性能瓶颈，Router层在设计上不直接执行具体任务，只负责人类交互与任务分派，甚至可以不配备Bash工具。

这种由一个中心节点分派多个执行节点的结构，表面上与常见Agent Team相似，但侧重点不同。常见Agent Team主要用于单个复杂任务内部的步骤拆解与角色协作，子步骤通常耦合较紧，Team Lead往往需要深入理解任务细节、规划子任务并高频协调成员，自身承担很重推理负载。而在Super-agent中，Router层只处理任务之间的高层关联与分派，无需介入单任务内部拆解。相反，如果通过提示词约束一个Agent Team的主会话不亲自执行具体任务，仅负责对外交互并将不同任务分派给各成员独立推进，也可以视为这种双层架构。团队实践显示，Router层任务常常没有想象中复杂，使用较轻量模型往往就能兼顾速度与效果。

内部实现上，Router层同样不必局限于单个Session，甚至部分逻辑未必需要调用LLM。团队选择最直接的单个常驻LLM Session作为Router层核心实现，并发现它并没有表面看起来那么容易成为吞吐瓶颈，因为上一轮推理期间到达的环境事件会积压下来、在下一轮一并处理，形成批处理，而合并处理的额外开销很小：

– 外部事件流平稳时，Trigger逐条进入Router Session，单次响应延迟较低；

– 事件密集涌入、Router Session出现排队拥堵时，上一轮推理期间积压的多条Trigger会自动合并，在下一次LLM调用中一并注入。Router Session只做轻量交互与分派，每步通常是长输入、短输出。把积压多条Trigger合并进一次LLM API调用，会在Prefill阶段并行计算，单次请求耗时增长远慢于批处理大小。因此在一定范围内，积压越多，单个决定分摊的推理时间越低；上限取决于上下文长度，以及模型在一轮中能准确处理多少条Trigger。

文章在后文通过实验定量展示批处理机制效果。加上订阅与直通机制以及链式召回，单个常驻Router Session在保持上下文连续的同时，在目前团队规模下已经够用。

当规模进一步扩大、单个会话确实不足以承载时，Router层内部也可设计为多层过滤结构，或水平切分为多个会话。此时Router层内部设计本质上是连续性与吞吐量的权衡。切分粒度越细，Router层并发吞吐量越高，但分片之间的记忆与上下文连续性越低。在全局记忆问题被解决前，这一权衡始终存在。

2、Worker层：只干活不抢话，冲突靠订阅同一Thread自己发现

Worker层由负责具体执行的会话组成，各Worker彼此上下文隔离，挂载完整执行工具，在独立上下文中专注完成单一任务。由于Worker Session直接决定任务结果与代码质量，通常需要配置能力最强的模型。

Worker不会直接与人类交互，其推理过程和工具调用不会直接输出到外部信道，而是向Router层汇报状态，由Router层统一向用户回复，从而在保障并发度与交付质量的同时避免多个会话各自回复带来混乱。

多任务并发执行时，各Worker独立推进任务，同层Worker之间通常不需要直接通信。多个Worker在具体执行中的冲突往往出现在同一个Pull Request等共享工作环境中；只要它们都订阅了对应Thread，就会收到相同事件通知，从而有机会自行发现和解决冲突，少数跨任务协同则由Router层中转。

与Router层类似，每个Worker Session内部也不必局限于单个会话：执行复杂单任务时，Worker内部可再创建Subagent，也可本身就是一个Agent Team，这些对上层的Router层保持透明。这一结构既适用于代码协作场景，同时推进多个独立问题复现、PR评审与特性开发而互不阻塞；也适用于个人助手场景：虽然个人助手界面上通常只提供一个单会话聊天页面，但当用户在同一对话框同时讨论多个不同话题时，前端单一聊天页负责维持交互连续性，底层可为每个话题分别分派Worker，并行推进任务、起草回复。

## 三、事件驱动：不等指令，环境事件当输入，四步让Agent主动干活

要让Super-agent具备主动性，首先需要改变系统驱动方式。驱动Agent的主要输入不再是人类在Session中逐条键入的提示词，而是环境中的半结构化事件。在Super-agent中，群聊消息、邮件与日程提醒、代码审查评论、CI运行结果等环境事件被称为Trigger。通过监听并响应Trigger，Agent不必再像单Session模式下那样，等人类下达指令才被动执行一次。

围绕一条环境事件从进入到处理的生命周期，文章依次讨论四个递进问题：如何通过程序与模型结合的两级策略过滤大量噪音；如何通过订阅与直通机制将事件路由给Worker；如何利用Inline & Spill与链式召回向模型高密度注入与按需召回上下文；如何利用投机执行根据环境信号在后台提前行动。

1、 事件过滤：程序先快筛，模型再慢判

接入真实群聊与代码平台后，环境事件流呈现显著“高噪音、低触发率”特征，绝大多数日常消息并不需要Agent介入。如果对每个事件都调用大模型从头判断，延迟和算力成本都难以承受。借鉴计算机系统中的Fast Path / Slow Path思想，大模型推理可看作灵活但高成本的Slow Path，而将已经明确且稳定的高频判断固化为确定性代码，则构成低延迟、低成本的Fast Path。

因此，事件进入系统后的第一步是过滤，目标是在调用大模型之前先用确定性策略筛除噪音，只将需要语义理解的候选事件交给模型判断。团队采用程序策略与大模型相结合的两级过滤机制：

– 程序层策略，作为Fast Path：针对事件来源、群组范围、用户或机器人白名单等确定性条件，直接通过代码进行快速准入检查，例如对不同来源分别设置“仅响应明确请求”“作为候选事件”或“直接忽略”，在调用模型前滤除大部分无关消息。

– 语义层策略，作为Slow Path：通过程序层准入的候选事件交给LLM，由它根据用提示词编写的策略和上下文判断是否需要行动。语义层同时作为面向人类的自然语言扩展点，方便随时通过提示词开关或新增策略。

▲两级过滤：先由程序层策略筛除大部分无关消息，再交由语义层策略判断

2、事件路由：后续事件不再绕Router，订阅了就直接发Worker

第2节引入的全局Router层负责维持跨信道连续性，但如果已分配任务的每个后续事件仍需经由Router层转发，这一全局节点依然会承受大量负载，推高系统响应延迟。因此，Fast / Slow Path同样适用于过滤后的事件路由。全局Router层仅负责新任务冷启动与跨任务协调，已确定归属关系的后续事件由程序直接发往对应Worker会话，无需经由Router层转发。

实际工作流中，同一个GitHub PR、同一个IM话题或同一封往来邮件串下的连续事件构成一条事件流，即Thread。

▲Thread示例：同一个IM话题或同一个GitHub Pull Request下的连续Trigger构成一条Thread

Router层根据某个Thread的初始事件创建Worker Session后，该Worker会直接订阅对应Thread，从而将事件路由分为两条路径：

– 已订阅，Fast Path：同一Thread下后续事件由程序直通已订阅Worker，无需Router层再次调用工具转发。若新事件超出当前任务范围，Worker也可取消订阅或交回Router层重新分派。

– 未订阅，Slow Path：Router层仍可观测所有事件以掌握全局状态，但仅负责判断和分派尚未被订阅的新事件。

▲订阅与直通：初始事件经由 Router 层创建 Worker 并建立订阅，同一 Thread 的后续事件直接发往该 Worker

此外，Thread与Worker之间的订阅是多对多关系。一个Worker可同时订阅多个相关Thread，同一个Thread也可被多个Worker订阅。当多个Worker在同一个工作环境或讨论中发生交集时，该Thread下新事件会同时直通给所有订阅它的Worker，使它们无需点对点通信，也有机会获知彼此操作并自行解决冲突。在输出侧，Worker仍将关键结论汇报给Router层，由Router层统一向用户回复并同步全局记忆。

3、上下文组织：常用直接放，长文先摘要，旧任务顺ID找

事件经过过滤与路由、进入目标Session后，下一个问题是应向模型上下文窗口注入多少信息。由于系统输入从有限人类提示词转向环境持续产生的半结构化事件，工具调用与事件注入的结构设计变得更加重要。注入过多会挤占窗口、稀释模型注意力，注入过少又会迫使模型反复调用工具读取，增加执行步数。文章直言：浪费上下文窗口，就是浪费模型的智能。

为此，可将有限上下文窗口当作Cache管理。借用编译优化与计算机系统概念，上下文注入设计可归纳为两个基本操作。Inline是指将近期很可能用到的信息直接内联进当前上下文窗口，以省去额外工具调用往返。Spill则是指将超出窗口预算或低频使用的完整信息留在上下文窗口之外，仅在窗口内保留引用或摘要，供模型按需读取。

结合计算机系统设计中经典的局部性思想，可用Inline & Spill对事件注入和工具调用逐步优化：

– 从最少信息开始：最初只提供当前对象ID和内容摘要。

– 利用局部性逐步Inline关联信息：将近期很可能用到的信息Inline到上下文中，先附上紧密关联对象ID，再附带时空相邻内容，例如内容前50字、IM消息前后相邻消息与所回复消息，或代码评论所在评审讨论中的相邻评论。

– 超出上限则Spill：对无法全部Inline的长内容设定较小长度上限，将超出部分Spill到窗口之外。一种简单直接做法是截断超出部分并保留续读入口，模型需要完整内容时再调用工具读取。

此外，在大量后续事件直通Worker、系统长期运行累积许多历史任务后，Router层既不能把所有任务全量历史都放入自己的上下文窗口，又需要在用户跨信道提起某个旧任务时找回上下文。将Inline & Spill一致应用到系统中各类对象后，就得到一种按需展开的多跳检索机制，即链式召回。这种链式召回缓解了Router层在长程中丢失先前信息的问题。

▲链式召回：每次召回的对象均内联下一跳关联对象的ID，支持沿引用关系逐跳展开上下文

具体来说，系统为Trigger、Thread和Worker Session等对象赋予唯一ID，并在注入时内联紧密关联对象ID，使这些对象在底层构成一张引用图。由于每一次调用工具召回的对象本身同样遵循Inline & Spill，其返回结果中又会内联下一跳关联对象的摘要与ID，模型便可以从当前事件出发，顺着引用关系逐步按需召回上下文。例如从一条当前消息读取所在Thread，再从Thread内联ID追踪到相关Worker Session，进而找到该Worker关联的另一个代码评审Thread。

4、提前行动：后台提前试，有价值才交付

借鉴计算机系统中的投机执行思想，Agent可以在还不确定结果是否会被采用时，根据环境信号在后台提前尝试，通过消耗额外后台算力减少人类等待与介入成本。结果有价值就交付，没有价值就丢弃。

在个人助手场景下，收到一封会议邀约邮件或待办消息时，Agent可先在后台核对日程冲突、搜集相关背景资料并备好回复草稿，待用户过目后直接确认发出。在研发协作场景下同样如此。例如团队在DeepSeek Harness内部用户群中配置了一条“静默复现并修复”策略：当群里有人反馈问题或讨论改动方案时，Agent先在后台尝试复现并寻找修复方案，只有在确认问题并找到简单修复方案后，才把结果交付给用户，否则全程保持安静。

▲投机执行示例：群内还在讨论解决方案时，Super-agent已在后台提交了修复Pull Request

## 四、 面向人的交互：全双工随时接新指令，多信道按人的习惯说话

双层架构保证了跨信道上下文连续，但实际交互体验还需解决两点：用异步ReAct Loop让后台耗时操作不阻塞前台，会话随时接受新指令；让输出方式匹配不同信道的带宽与人的使用习惯。

1、全双工交互：后台干活，前台不卡，新指令随时进

经典ReAct Loop中，模型发起一次同步的run()工具调用后，循环会阻塞，直到工具执行完毕并返回最终结果，在此期间会话无法响应任何新的用户输入。要消除这一阻塞，需要将对话从一问一答的半双工模式转变为全双工模式。

▲经典ReAct Loop与异步ReAct Loop对比

为此，团队将耗时命令与子任务工具调用改为异步的start()和stop()，构成异步ReAct Loop。模型调用start()后立即收到“已启动”返回，循环不再等待该工具；后台工具执行完成后，系统再将最终结果作为一条新事件消息投递进会话；同时，模型也可根据上下文调用stop()主动终止执行时间过长的后台命令。

由此，前台对话响应与后台任务执行得以解耦，Agent在后台运行耗时任务的同时也能响应人类输入。新输入在当前推理步结束后即被处理，不必等待后台工具完成。文章透露，这一异步任务机制已在DeepSeek Harness中实现，但尚未默认开启。

2、多信道交互：群聊低打扰短回复，PR邮件高密度写完整

不同工作信道具有不同信息密度与交互习惯，系统输出需要与之匹配。如果将面向单人终端的交互方式直接搬入群聊，把冗长推理过程与密集工具调用原样输出，在多人协作中极易造成信息过载。

在Super-agent中，双层架构已解决其中一部分问题：具体任务中冗长推理过程和密集工具调用都被隔离在Worker Session内部，不会直接输出到外部信道，而由Router层统一负责对外交互。在此基础上，系统还需接入用户日常使用的各类工作环境，并通过提示词针对不同信道定制交互规范：

– IM等即时通讯信道：侧重低打扰的轻量沟通，像人类同事一样只在需要决策或验收时发送通知，只问直接问题、给简短结论。团队验证过一条简单有效的硬性规定：单次回复不超过100词。

– GitHub、邮件与文档等异步信道：侧重结构化、高信息密度的异步交付，例如创建或更新Pull Request时按项目规范撰写完整问题背景、改动说明与验证结果，或在个人助

# Qwen3.8抢先体验！大家要心理准备了，最新版发布并开源了？

2026-10-31 6

举报

简介： 2026年8月，阿里通义千问Qwen3.8系列全线开源，涵盖2.4万亿参数旗舰Max、27B轻量版、Flash高效模型及Flash-Next预览版。支持本地部署、多模态与长上下文，Apache 2.0（27B）与分层商用许可并行，标志国产大模型迈入“可下载、可部署、可商用”新阶段。（239字）

### Qwen3.8全线开源：国产大模型进入“旗舰可下载、本地可部署、商用有门槛”的新阶段

2026年8月，阿里通义千问Qwen3.8系列正式开源。

开源活动（链接入口）：https://www.aliyun.com/product/tongyi

到10月下旬，从2.4万亿参数旗舰到27B轻量版，再到Flash效率模型和Flash-Next预览版，整个系列已经全部开放。

这轮发布不是简单“又多了一个模型”，而是把能力上限、本地落地、推理成本和商业规则一次性补齐。对开发者来说，它意味着国产大模型从“能跑”真正走到了“能用、能部署、能商用”。

## 一、Qwen3.8-Max：旗舰能力第一次开放权重

Qwen3.8-Max总参数2.4万亿，采用稀疏MoE架构，每次推理激活约950亿参数，支持最长100万Token上下文，原生多模态。它最突出的变化是编程和Agent能力。演示中，它可以从空文件夹出发，连续运行多日，独立完成一个自进化智能体框架项目。

9月2日发布的0902版本是一次明显增强。它在编程和办公场景上做了后训练优化，TerminalBench从11.3提升到29.0，DeepSWE从56.6提升到69.3，QwenSWEBench从55.1提升到70.0。在CodeArena前端编程总榜中，0902版本以1691分登顶，超过Claude Opus 5、Kimi K3等模型。API定价为输入2美元/百万Token、输出6美元/百万Token，综合平均约5美元/百万Token，性价比优势明显。

需要特别注意的是，Qwen3.8-Max虽然开放了权重，但并不等于云端服务的全部能力一起打包。开源版本主要是纯文本权重，云端API还包含视觉输入、工具调用、内置搜索、非思考模式等增强能力。所以本地部署和云端调用之间，体验会有差异。

## 二、Qwen3.8-27B：个人和本地部署的“甜点模型”

Qwen3.8-27B是270亿参数稠密模型，Apache 2.0协议，原生上下文262K，可外推到1M。它是这轮开源里最适合个人开发者、中小企业和本地部署的版本。

量化后，INT4版本权重大约14-17GB。RTX 4060 Ti 16G可以跑，但上下文需要控制；RTX 3090/4090 24G会更从容，能支持更长上下文和更高并发。它支持Ollama、llama.cpp、vLLM、SGLang等主流推理框架，部署路径比较成熟。

能力上，27B并不弱。SWE-bench Pro得分61.7，Terminal Bench 2.1达到73.0，编程、办公、长上下文处理都有明显提升。它还是原生多模态，能直接理解图像、视频和文本，不再需要单独拼接视觉模块。对做私有知识库、代码辅助、内部工具、本地Agent的开发者来说，27B是目前最值得尝试的开源模型之一。

## 三、Qwen3.8-Flash：把推理成本打下来

Qwen3.8-Flash总参数125B，但每次只激活约6B，训练成本较前代降低近90%。它引入QSA稀疏注意力机制，1M长上下文场景下预填充和解码速度都有明显提升。API定价低至输入1元/百万Token、输出3元/百万Token，适合高并发、客服、摘要、工具调用等场景。

同月开源的Qwen3.8-Flash-Next则是下一代Qwen4架构的预览版，但它使用的是Qwen Community License 1.0，和27B的Apache 2.0不同，商用时需要单独核对授权。

## 四、许可证变化：开源不再是“无条件免费”

这是本轮发布最容易被忽略、也最值得重视的一点。

Qwen3.8-27B仍采用Apache 2.0，允许免费商用、修改、微调和私有化部署，没有营收门槛。但Qwen3.8-Max采用专用Qwen3.8-Max License：如果经营MaaS或AI Work Assistant业务，且连续12个月集团收入超过5000万美元，商用前需另行授权；产品月活超过1亿或月收入超过2000万美元，还需在界面显著标注模型名称。Flash-Next的Qwen Community License 1.0更严格，只要从事MaaS或AI Work Assistant业务，就需要单独授权。

对云厂商、模型聚合平台、AI编程助手、办公助手类产品的商业化团队来说，这些条款需要法务介入评估；但对大多数个人开发者、研究团队和中小企业的内部使用，影响不大。

## 五、怎么选？

场景 | 推荐版本 | 关键理由 
---|---|---
复杂编程、长周期Agent、企业级任务 | Qwen3.8-Max-0902 | 编程和办公能力最强，API性价比高 
高并发、成本敏感、客服与摘要 | Qwen3.8-Flash | 激活参数小，推理成本低 
本地部署、数据不出域、私有知识库 | Qwen3.8-27B | Apache 2.0，消费级显卡可跑 
探索下一代架构 | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | Qwen4雏形，但授权更严格 

## 六、这轮开源意味着什么

Qwen3.8系列的最大价值，是把国产大模型的三条路径同时打通了：Max代表能力上限，Flash代表效率下限，27B代表本地落地。它不再是“参数好看但用不起来”，而是真正进入了可部署、可微调、可商用、可验证的阶段。

当然，开放权重不等于人人都能轻松跑旗舰。2.4T模型需要多节点集群，27B也需要合理显存规划。许可证也不再是单纯的Apache 2.0，商用边界需要仔细看。但正因为这些规则写清楚了，开发者反而能更安心地选择：想做实验用27B，想压成本用Flash，想追上限用Max，想做私有化就用本地部署。

对开发者来说，接下来最值得关注的有三件事：社区基于27B能做出哪些实用工具；Flash-Next代表的Qwen4架构何时正式落地；以及国产大模型在编程、Agent和长上下文场景上，还能把体验推到什么程度。

相关文章

### 大模型

# 阿里巴巴凌晨重磅官宣：与Apple达成合作，将千问集成至Apple智能，中国用户可以在Siri等中直接调用千问的文本与图像理解、内容生成等能力

杭州网 发布时间：2026-10-31 09:52

今后，可以用Siri喊“千问”了。

10月31日，阿里巴巴宣布与 Apple达成合作，将千问集成至 Apple 智能，中国用户可以在Siri、写作工具及视觉智能中，直接调用千问的文本与图像理解、内容生成等能力。这些功能将于11月4日起随最新的iOS 开发者 Beta 版开放测试，并将于12月iOS 27.3正式发布时面向中国用户推出。

Siri可以直接调用千问的广博知识，并在 Siri 中直接回复用户问答。通过 Siri，用户还能用自己选择的文档和照片，直接向千问提问。在任何问题、文档和图片发送给千问之前，都会先征得用户同意。

千问也已接入Apple 的系统级写作工具中，为用户提供“千问创作”（Compose with Qwen）功能。“千问创作”可以帮助用户基于任意主题生成内容。用户还可以使用这一功能来生成图像。

在 iPhone 上，用户可以通过视觉智能功能更深入地了解周围环境，其中包括选择“询问千问”来识别眼前所见。用户可通过相机控制、操作按钮或控制中心来启用视觉智能功能。

用户可以自主选择是否开通千问集成功能。启用后，用户可通过 Apple 登录或使用自己的千问 App 账户登录，在 Siri、写作工具和视觉智能中使用千问。用户可以自主决定何时使用千问，以及分享哪些信息。用户请求及生成的回复均不会被阿里巴巴用于模型训练，以保护用户隐私。

目前，千问的集成功能将在 iOS中提供，面向在中国购买了支持 Apple 智能的 iPhone用户，或设备定位和 Apple 账户国家/地区均设置在中国的用户。

阿里巴巴集团CEO吴泳铭表示：“我们很高兴与苹果公司达成合作。千问将依托阿里巴巴深厚的AI 技术积淀，深度融入苹果生态系统的各项体验，共同为中国苹果用户带来全新的智能服务。”

GLM.content:
# Open-weight GLM 5.3 autonomously exploits six Firefox releases

Research group Epoch AI published a report on Oct. 30 saying that GLM 5.3, the model Zhipu AI open-sourced in August, autonomously wrote attack code against Firefox in its experiments. All six stable Firefox releases shipped between Sept. 17 and Oct. 26 were compromised.

The effect: a user opens a malicious web page in Firefox, and with no clicks at all, local files are read out and sent to the attacker. The vulnerability leads the model used came from security fixes that Mozilla had already made public but had not yet shipped in a stable release.

## How the patch gap gets exploited

Epoch calls this kind of attack exploiting the "patch gap." Once a security fix for an open-source project is committed to a public repository, an attacker can work backward from the diff to find the underlying bug, while ordinary users' stable builds take a while to receive the fix.

The experiment deliberately modeled an attacker with limited resources and modest skill, giving the model only the public information available at the time of each release. Each attempt was capped at 48 hours, and the fastest success took about 12 hours. In one case the model opened a foothold using the fix record for a memory bug; after Firefox's defenses blocked file access, it chained together several further steps on its own.

Attacks on the most recent releases went a step further: the model chained one patch-gap bug with another vulnerability that had not yet been disclosed. The latter was fixed in Firefox 159.0, released on Oct. 27. Epoch's report cites Mozilla security advisory mfsa2026-118 and does not list a CVE number.

"We did not trigger any safeguards or refusals from any provider, including Z.ai, when using GLM 5.3 in this way."

The report does not mention any response from Zhipu.

## Firefox and Chrome came out differently

The same approach did not succeed against Chrome, even though Epoch also spent about $100,000 in compute on Chrome. The researchers specifically caution that this should not be read as strong evidence that Chrome is more secure: better prompts, or a stronger open-weight model, could change the outcome.

On cost, the Firefox work as a whole consumed more than $100,000 in API fees, most of it going to building the offline test environment and early trial and error. Once the environment was in place, each version cost roughly $1,000 to attack.

What sets this apart from closed models is that the weights are public. Anthropic's Mythos has also been used for vulnerability discovery before, and the report notes that Mythos can decompile Windows binaries to read out patch contents, but closed models have provider-side screening and refusal mechanisms that can stop misuse. Anyone can download GLM 5.3's weights and run them locally, beyond the reach of provider-level safeguards. The report adds that the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro are expected in early November, and early testing suggests it may be stronger than GLM 5.3 at this kind of work.

## The researchers' recommendations and caveats

Epoch makes three recommendations: keep security fixes private until they are ready to ship; move changes from beta to stable faster; and avoid patching several chainable vulnerabilities at once. Firefox and Chrome both ship weekly now, and the researchers think even that pace may not be fast enough.

The report also has clear limits. All experiments ran in an offline simulation the researchers built themselves, and no real users were attacked on a live network. Success rates are tallied per version, with no larger-sample analysis, and the authors state plainly that they draw no conclusions about how open-weight models will reshape the balance between attackers and defenders. Whether an open-weight model can decompile the binaries of closed-source software to read patches was not tested this time.

Sources: Epoch AI research report (affected version range, per-attempt duration and API costs); CocoLoop; Mozilla security advisory (Firefox 159.0 fix record).

GLM.content:
# AIcoding 商业化 2026：GLM-5.2 通过率数据背后的投入产出账

某零售客户 CTO 问我们：Cursor、Claude Code、ZCode 都买齐了，团队效率怎么没涨？这是 2026 年被问得最多的问题。ZCode 针对 GLM-5.2 深度优化，上线 Goal、Subagents、Remote Control、闲时任务四大功能；在 Z.ai Code Bench 里，GLM-5.2 搭配 ZCode 比搭配 Claude Code 任务整体通过率高 2.39%，缓存命中率超 98%，额度使用量约 1.8 倍。工具性能在涨，企业的投入产出却未必。

## 通过率数据怎么读：2.39% 不等于交付质量

官方评测数据本身没问题，但要用对位置。Z.ai Code Bench 测的是模型加工具组合能不能把任务跑通，衡量的颗粒度是单元级与仓库级任务。交付项目时，我们更关心代码评审通过率、线上故障率、返工工时。这两套指标体系经常脱节：测试路径写错、琐碎任务占多数、评测集被模型刷过，都会虚高通过率。

指标 | benchmark 看什么 | 交付看什么 
---|---|---
通过率 | 任务能否跑通 | 代码能否上生产 
缓存命中率 | 额度成本 | 团队等待时间 
额度使用量 | API 成本 | 单功能开发成本 
测试路径 | 自动化断言 | 真实业务边界 

2.39% 的优势落到交付上，可能是少返工两个版本，也可能毫无感知。先定义自己的衡量口径，再谈工具选型，别把评测榜当交付保证。模型行为边界往往藏在系统提示词里，Claude Opus 5 系统提示词泄露解读里我们拆过这个问题：榜单数字之外，提示词工程与工具行为边界才更影响实际交付。这一点和选型文章里我们坚持的结论一致：Claude Code 与 GLM-5.2 的实测对比只解决工具层问题，解决不了流程层问题。

## AIcoding 商业化的三条路径

AIcoding 商业化不是同一个动作，至少有三条路径，投入和回收周期完全不同。

- 内部提效：把 AI 编程工具引入现有研发团队，目标是把单功能开发成本降下来。投入是订阅费加培训，回收按月算。
- 对外交付：用 AIcoding 团队接定制项目，把人力杠杆变现。这是我们 2026 年主要在做的事，回收按项目算。
- 产品化：把 AI 编程能力沉淀成可重复交付的 SaaS 或行业方案，回收按年算，但前期投入最大。

三条路径可以叠加，但建议先走通一条再扩。我们见过最典型的失败：一上来三条路同时铺，三个月后哪条都没跑通。

## 从 8 周交付项目看 AIcoding 团队人效

2026 年上半年，我们交付了一个某零售行业客户的数字化项目：40 多个业务模块、60 个接口。传统外包估算是 12 人 8 周，我们实际用 3 人加 AI 编程在 8 周内交付。

人效提升不是把 12 人换成 3 人这么简单，关键是流程变了：

- 需求先拆成可验证的单元，交给 AI 编码；
- 每两小时一次增量评审，错误在 30 分钟内被发现；
- 构建从 12 分钟压到 3 分钟，反馈循环缩短。

12 到 3 的数字好看，真正省下的是返工成本，不是人头。这个判断和用 AI 编程重构交付团队那篇的结论相互印证：初级程序员岗位在收缩，剩下的岗位在重新定义。

## 算账模型：工具订阅 vs 人力成本 vs 返工成本

给决策者一个可以直接套的算账框架，按年算。以一支 3 人高级团队为例：

成本项 | 传统团队 | AIcoding 团队 
---|---|---
人力成本（3 名高级 × 50 万） | 150 万 | 150 万 
工具订阅（席位 × 年费） | 0 | 6-12 万 
返工与质量成本 | 20-40 万 | 5-10 万 
年总成本 | 170-190 万 | 161-172 万 

这个模型的关键结论：工具订阅是最小的一笔钱。决定 ROI 正负的是流程改造能力和返工成本。订阅单价本身还在快速变化，Kimi K3 发布后的三工具成本重算里我们的结论是：成本结构每季度都要重算一次，别拿半年前的报价当今年的预算。Google 在 Helpful Content 官方文档里反复强调为搜索而非为读者生产的内容会被降权，企业用 AI 编程同理——为省事而堆代码，最后一定为返工买单。如果只买工具不改造流程，AI 生成的代码会变成新的技术债。

## 反面教训：不改造流程只堆工具，ROI 为负

我们一开始也犯过这个错。2025 年某项目团队直接上了 3 个 AI 编程工具，没有改评审机制，一个季度后代码库出现大量重复代码，测试覆盖率反而下降。工具订阅花了钱，返工还多了，ROI 为负。

后来我们把流程改掉：AI 只负责从需求到可验证代码，人负责拆需求、评审、上线。同一个工具组合，交付周期缩短了 40%。工具是杠杆，流程是支点，没有支点，杠杆越大越危险。

## 常见问题

### AIcoding 商业化是不是就是买 Claude Code 或 ZCode 会员？

不是。订阅只是入场券，商业化的核心是流程改造和交付体系。工具性能差异远小于流程好坏造成的差距。

### GLM-5.2 和 Claude Code 怎么选？

团队主要用国内模型、有合规要求，GLM-5.2 搭配 ZCode 更顺；已有 Claude Code 工作流的团队要考虑迁移成本。建议先定流程，再定工具。

### 3 人 AIcoding 团队真的能顶 12 人吗？

需求清晰、接口明确、评审及时的项目里可以接近这个效率；需求含糊、领域复杂、合规要求高的项目里人效优势会缩小。别拿特例当通用结论。

### 小团队适合走哪条商业化路径？

3-10 人团队建议从内部提效或对外交付里选一条，先跑通算账模型，再考虑产品化。

如果你也在算 AI 编程的投入产出，欢迎带着项目规模和成本结构来找我们聊，先出算账模型再决定要不要动。联系蓝曜炬辉（广州市蓝曜炬辉科技有限公司）获取 AIcoding 转型咨询，也可以先看完整案例库。

GLM.content:
# 亚马逊将中国AI模型Kimi、GLM引入云服务

亚马逊已在其AI平台上新增由Bedrock托管的中国Kimi和GLM开源模型版本。首席执行官安迪·贾西(Andy Jassy)表示,西方客户同样希望获得更多西方打造的开源模型。他是在10月29日(周四)的第三季度财报电话会议上披露这些新增模型的。根据电话会议记录,他还表示Bedrock目前也提供OpenAI模型和SpaceXAI模型。

贾西说:“我认为西方世界非常渴望获得更多西方开源模型,因此我相信随着时间推移,这种情况也会出现。”他还补充说,“Bedrock的市场机会十分巨大,它有可能成长为与EC2一样庞大的服务。”EC2是亚马逊云科技(AWS)的核心计算服务。以上内容出自Investing.com发布的电话会议记录。

# 多模型押注

Benzinga 报道称,Bedrock 上的开放模型包括月之暗面的 Kimi K3 和智谱(Z.ai)的 GLM 5.3,与 Anthropic、OpenAI 的闭源模型并列其中。该媒体称,智谱的 GLM 5.3 于 10 月初登陆 Bedrock,主打智能体编程和复杂软件工程场景。

贾西认为,没有哪一款模型能一家独大。据雅虎财经报道,他说:"我认为未来会有六到八款模型,彼此水平相当,或者至少能满足 95% 以上工作负载的需求。"他表示,客户希望有丰富的模型可选,这样在这些模型"你追我赶、交替领先"时,就能随时切换。根据文字记录,他还强调,Bedrock 的输入和输出内容"绝不会与模型提供方共享,也不会用于训练基础模型"。对于正在权衡是否使用中国开发的模型的企业来说,这一点至关重要。

# Bedrock 的快速增长

贾西称,Bedrock 是亚马逊云科技(AWS)历史上增长最快的百亿美元级服务。据雅虎财经整理的电话会议要点,他表示,财富 500 强企业在该服务上的支出比一年前增长了近 6 倍,令牌总量增长了近 16 倍。根据会议记录,他还表示,Bedrock 目前大部分业务已运行在亚马逊自研的 Trainium 芯片上,并称这些芯片带来了更高的性价比和更好的利润率。

亚马逊公布的第三季度营收为 2019 亿美元,同比增长 12%,营业利润为 281 亿美元。不过,据 Investing.com 报道,每股收益未达预期,盘后股价下跌。据 Benzinga 报道,周五盘前交易时段,该股继续走低。

# 中国开源模型加速崛起

此举正值中国开放权重模型的应用日益广泛之际。据 Benzinga 报道,谷歌前 CEO 埃里克·施密特(Eric Schmidt)上周表示,中国在人工智能领域大约落后美国六个月,但他同时警告说,廉价甚至免费的开源模型可能帮助中国企业赢得发展中国家市场。7 月,英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋称中国的模型"非常出色",并主张华盛顿方面应当利用高质量的开源技术,而不是禁止它。

这让亚马逊处境略显尴尬:其 CEO 一边呼吁西方推出更多开源模型,另一边公司却在向眼下就需要开源选项的客户出售中国模型。

Kimi.title: Moonshot (Kimi) | Promptfoo
Kimi.description: Moonshot (Kimi) Moonshot AI provides an OpenAI-compatible API for its Kimi models — the Kimi K3 and K2 thinking models and the Moonshot v1 generation models. ... - Kimi K3 — flagship thinking model, 1M context ... - Kimi K2 — thinking models, 256k context...
Kimi.content:
# Moonshot (Kimi)

Moonshot AI provides an OpenAI-compatible API for its Kimi models — the Kimi K3 and K2 thinking models and the Moonshot v1 generation models. The Moonshot provider extends the OpenAI provider, so all of its options are supported.

## Setup

- Get an API key from the Kimi (Moonshot) platform.
- Set theMOONSHOT_API_KEY environment variable or specify apiKey in your config.

Kimi K3 requires a successful account top-up of at least $1; see the access requirements.
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3

Bothmoonshot:<model> and moonshot:chat:<model> resolve to the chat completions endpoint. If you omit the model, the provider defaults to kimi-k3.

## Available Models

Moonshot's lineup rotates over time — call the list models API (GET https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/models) for the live set. As of writing:

- Kimi K3 — flagship thinking model, 1M context:kimi-k3 (released July 2026). Always-on reasoning, native image and video understanding, and a top-level reasoning_effort control (see below).
- Kimi K2 — thinking models, 256k context:kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed. These reason before answering and emit a separate reasoning stream (see below).
- Moonshot v1 — legacy generation models:moonshot-v1-8k, moonshot-v1-32k, moonshot-v1-128k (context-length variants) and the vision variants moonshot-v1-8k-vision-preview / moonshot-v1-32k-vision-preview / moonshot-v1-128k-vision-preview; existing accounts may also see the auto-router moonshot-v1-auto in the list-models API. The moonshot-v1 series and kimi-k2.5 are closed to newly registered users and sunset platform-wide on August 31, 2026.

The olderkimi-k2-0711-preview, kimi-k2-0905-preview, kimi-k2-turbo-preview, kimi-k2-thinking, kimi-k2-thinking-turbo, and kimi-latest ids were discontinued in 2026 — Moonshot recommends migrating to kimi-k3.

## Configuration
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3 # flagship thinking model — leave sampling params unset
  - id: moonshot:moonshot-v1-8k # legacy generation model — accepts arbitrary sampling
    config:
      temperature: 0.2
      max_tokens: 1024

### Configuration Options

The provider accepts every option the OpenAI provider supports. Commonly used:

- temperature, max_tokens, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty
- stream
- response_format (JSON mode), tools / tool_choice (function calling)
- showThinking — set to false to drop a thinking model's reasoning from the graded output (default true)
- cost, inputCost, outputCost, cacheReadCost — Moonshot ships no built-in price table, so set these to track cost. Every override is in USD per token. Moonshot's official pricing page publishes rates in USD per 1 million tokens, so divide each published rate by 1,000,000 before configuring it. inputCost/outputCost take precedence over the flat cost; cacheReadCost prices cached prompt tokens.

For example, these illustrative per-million rates convert to per-token overrides. Check the official pricing page for the current rates for your model before using them.
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
    config:
      inputCost: 0.000003 # $3.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      cacheReadCost: 0.0000003 # $0.30 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      outputCost: 0.000015 # $15.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k2.6
    config:
      inputCost: 0.00000095 # $0.95 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      cacheReadCost: 0.00000016 # $0.16 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      outputCost: 0.000004 # $4.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000

Any other parameter supported by the OpenAI provider is forwarded as-is.

## Kimi thinking models

Thekimi-k3 and kimi-k2.x models are reasoning models and behave differently from the moonshot-v1 family:

- Fixed sampling parameters. Kimi pinstemperature (1.0 with thinking on), top_p, n, and the penalties to fixed values and returns a 400 ("invalid temperature: only 1 is allowed for this model") for any other value. The provider therefore does not send promptfoo's default temperature/max_tokens for kimi-* models — leave them unset (recommended) or set temperature: 1. The moonshot-v1 models accept arbitrary sampling values.
- Reasoning output. Kimi returns a separatereasoning_content stream that promptfoo surfaces with a Thinking: … prefix. Set showThinking: false when you assert on structured output (for example is-json) so the reasoning doesn't contaminate the parsed result.
- Token budget. Reasoning tokens count against the output budget. When you leave the token limit unset the provider lets Moonshot apply its server default (32k for K2.x, 131k for K3); if you set one, leave generous headroom for the answer. Moonshot's canonical field ismax_completion_tokens (max_tokens is a deprecated alias) — the provider sends max_completion_tokens for kimi-* models whichever of the two you configure.
- Controlling thinking. The two generations use different, mutually exclusive controls:
- kimi-k3 is always thinking and accepts a top-level reasoning_effort field, which the provider forwards from config.reasoning_effort. Supported values are low, high, and max (the default). Do not send the K2.x thinking parameter to K3 — the API rejects it.
- kimi-k2.6 and kimi-k2.5 support thinking: { type: disabled } (pass it via config.passthrough); kimi-k2.7-code is always thinking. The thinking parameter is K2.x-only.
- Settingconfig.reasoning_effort on a non-K3 model is a configuration error and the provider fails fast with a clear message instead of sending it.

providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
    config:
      showThinking: false
      reasoning_effort: max # optional: low, high, or max (default)
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k2.6
    config:
      passthrough:
        thinking: { type: disabled } # K2.x only: turn reasoning off

See the Kimi K3 quickstart and Using Thinking Models for the full behavior matrix.

## Vision

The vision models (moonshot-v1-*-vision-preview) and the multimodal Kimi models (kimi-k3, kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed) accept base64-encoded image input using the standard OpenAI image_url content format. Moonshot does not accept remote image URLs — embed images as data: URIs or reference files uploaded to the Kimi platform as ms://<file-id>. Video input is supported by kimi-k3, kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, and kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed, referenced the same way after uploading via the files API. See Use the Kimi Vision Model.

## Example Usage
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
  - id: openai:gpt-4o-mini

prompts:
  - 'Summarize the following in one sentence: {{text}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      text: 'Promptfoo is an open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM apps.'

A runnable comparison lives in examples/provider-moonshot.

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 (global). China-mainland keys use https://api.moonshot.cn/v1 — point at it with apiBaseUrl, since the global and China platforms issue region-locked keys.
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions API.
- Full API documentation.

## See Also

- OpenAI Provider — compatible configuration options
- Kimi model list and pricing

Kimi.title: GPT-6 Astra Distillation: DeepSeek, Moonshot Named in Report
Kimi.description: The report names Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro ... Moonshot said Kimi K3.1 Pro beat GPT-6 Astra on a coding benchmark, while DeepSeek has pitched V4.1-Flash as a low-cost alternative to US models.
Kimi.content:
# GPT-6 Astra Distillation: DeepSeek, Moonshot Named in Report

DeepSeek and Moonshot AI reportedly used GPT-6 Astra distillation to train Kimi K3.1 Pro and V4.1-Flash, The Information says. What is known so far.

Chinese AI labs DeepSeek and Moonshot AI leaned heavily on GPT-6 Astra distillation to train their newest models, according to a report published by The Information on October 28, citing people with direct knowledge of the matter. The report names Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro, released on October 23, and DeepSeek’s upgraded V4.1-Flash 1017, launched on October 17.

None of the three companies has confirmed the claim. OpenAI, DeepSeek and Moonshot AI did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters, and no logs, account details or data volumes have been made public.

## What GPT-6 Astra Distillation Means

Distillation is a training shortcut. A developer sends a large number of prompts to a stronger model, collects its answers and uses them as training data for its own system. Done at scale, it lets a cheaper model reproduce part of a frontier model’s abilities without the same research and compute budget. Using OpenAI’s outputs this way to build a competing model breaks the company’s terms of service.

Both Chinese models have posted strong scores in their makers’ own tests. Moonshot said Kimi K3.1 Pro beat GPT-6 Astra on a coding benchmark, while DeepSeek has pitched V4.1-Flash as a low-cost alternative to US models. Neither result has been independently verified.

## OpenAI Already Pointed at Moonshot in September

The new report builds on an earlier accusation. In a September 30 blog post, OpenAI said it disrupted a coordinated campaign to extract the protected reasoning of its models. The activity started on July 1, spiked on July 24 and 25 with 16,000 requests from more than 4,000 users, and was linked to a wider cluster of more than 15,000 users before OpenAI shut it down by July 28.

OpenAI said it could not tie every operator to a single actor, but it attributed “a core cluster of the activity to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, the developer of Kimi.” The company said the operators did not break its encryption or reach stored user conversations. It banned accounts, closed the replay pathway and shared its findings through the Frontier Model Forum. Moonshot has previously denied that its earlier Kimi K3 model was built through distillation.

## Why It Matters

Distillation has become one of the sharpest points of friction in the US and China AI race. Anthropic accused Chinese labs of distilling Claude in September, and on October 12 it said new safeguards had cut the reasoning data harvested by distillers by about 90% to 99%, according to its distillation defenses post.

For OpenAI, the stakes are commercial as well as political. The company is raising money at a reported $1.25 trillion valuation, and its pitch rests on keeping a lead with models such as GPT-6 Astra and the newer GPT-6.1 Terra. If rivals can copy those gains cheaply through API access, that lead narrows fast. For now, the claim against DeepSeek and Moonshot rests on anonymous sources, and we will update this story if any of the companies responds.

Kimi.content:
# Moonshot AI unveils Kimi K3.1 Pro model

Moonshot AI has moved its Kimi model family deeper into the global frontier-AI race, unveiling Kimi K3.1 Pro with a 1-million-token context window and saying it will release the full model weights by Nov. 4.

The launch matters because it is another sign that Chinese AI developers are pushing open-weight models toward capabilities once associated mainly with the best closed systems from US rivals. Moonshot said the new model is its most capable 3T-class open-weight release yet, with upgrades in coding, financial research, 3D creation and other agentic tasks. That expands the strategic value of open models for enterprises that want to run them privately, fine-tune them internally or deploy them at lower cost than proprietary alternatives.

Moonshot is also using scale and transparency as part of its competitive pitch. The company said K3.1 Pro was trained with significantly greater compute during post-training and that it has improved its reinforcement learning framework, long-context handling and infrastructure. The model is now live across Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code and the Kimi API, while a high-speed version offers 2-3 times faster response times for more interactive use cases.

The benchmark claims are aimed squarely at the market’s most closely watched comparison set: coding agents and enterprise automation. Moonshot said K3.1 Pro scored 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, ahead of GPT-6 Astra’s 58.2% and close to Claude Opus 5.5’s 66.4%, while its own Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon score rose to 61.2% from 55.95% for K3. For investors, that is the key question: whether Chinese open models are reaching a level where performance no longer lags enough to block commercial adoption.

The broader economic implication is pressure on the premium attached to proprietary AI platforms and the chip-and-cloud stack that supports them. If open-weight Chinese models become more capable and more widely distributed, they can accelerate enterprise adoption in Asia and beyond, but they may also intensify competition on pricing, inference demand and model access. That is relevant to cloud providers, AI software vendors and chipmakers such as Nvidia, whose shares have been trading below the 50-day moving average and near the lower end of recent technical ranges after a sharp pullback from summer highs.

Chinese AI names also stand to benefit from the local momentum. Alibaba’s U.S.-listed shares and the broader KWEB internet ETF have both weakened recently, but Moonshot’s release reinforces the case that China’s AI ecosystem remains active despite US export controls and broader tech tensions. In that sense, the story is not just about one model launch; it is about China’s attempt to prove that it can build frontier-grade systems on its own terms, with open distribution as a strategic advantage.

For investors, the next catalyst is the November weight release. If Moonshot makes the full model available as promised, developers will be able to test whether the benchmark gains hold up in real-world deployment. That will help determine whether Kimi K3.1 Pro becomes another reference point in China’s AI upcycle — or simply another headline in an increasingly crowded race.

Entity | Gains | Losses 
---|---|---
Moonshot AI | ▲Wider adoption; stronger credibility | ▼Higher compute and release risk 
Chinese AI ecosystem | ▲More competitive open models | ▼Pressure to keep pace on scale 
Enterprise users | ▲Lower-cost model access | ▼Greater vendor-switching complexity 
Proprietary AI rivals | ▲Benchmark pressure to innovate | ▼Pricing and moat pressure

xAI.title: Output Watermarking | SpaceXSI Docs
xAI.description: Text responses from supported Grok models include an invisible watermark. The watermark lets SpaceXSI later recognize text as model-generated, and it requires no change to your requests: there is no parameter to send ... xai.responses('grok-4.7'), prompt: 'Write a haiku about the ocean.'...
xAI.content:
#### Advanced API Usage

# Output Watermarking

Text responses from supported Grok models include an invisible watermark. The watermark lets SpaceXSI later recognize text as model-generated, and it requires no change to your requests: there is no parameter to send, and your integration works the same way with or without it.

SpaceXSI watermarks text model output to comply with the EU AI Act. The watermark is enabled on every SpaceXSI API endpoint, including the global endpoint,https://api.x.ai, and any regional endpoint.

Watermarking is controlled per model for your whole team. Team admins can opt out in the SpaceXSI Console; see Opting out.

## Which outputs are watermarked

Watermarking applies to text output from text generation requests, for each model that has watermarking turned on for your team.

Starting November 7, 2026, responses from these models include a watermark. It's on by default, and you can opt out per model.

- grok-4.7
- grok-4.6
- grok-4.5
- grok-4.3
- grok-4.20-reasoning
- grok-4.20-non-reasoning
- grok-4.20-multi-agent

Watermarking applies to outputs from every text generation API, including the Responses API and the Chat Completions API. It covers the generated text you receive in the response: ordinary text responses, structured outputs, and tool call arguments.

### Checking whether a response was watermarked

To check whether a response was watermarked, read thex-watermark header on the Responses API or Chat Completions API response. x-watermark: true means the output for that request was generated with the watermark. Any other value, or no header at all, means it was not.
import { xai } from '@ai-sdk/xai';
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const { text, response } = await generateText({
  model: xai.responses('grok-4.7'),
  prompt: 'Write a haiku about the ocean.',
});

console.log(response.headers?.['x-watermark']);
console.log(text);
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.getenv("XAI_API_KEY"),
    base_url="https://api.x.ai/v1",
)

raw = client.responses.with_raw_response.create(
    model="grok-4.7",
    input="Write a haiku about the ocean.",
)
response = raw.parse()

print(raw.headers.get("x-watermark"))
print(response.output_text)
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.XAI_API_KEY,
  baseURL: 'https://api.x.ai/v1',
});

const { data: response, response: raw } = await client.responses
  .create({
    model: 'grok-4.7',
    input: 'Write a haiku about the ocean.',
  })
  .withResponse();

console.log(raw.headers.get('x-watermark'));
console.log(response.output_text);
curl -i https://api.x.ai/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $XAI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "grok-4.7",
    "input": "Write a haiku about the ocean."
  }'

## How it works

The watermark is not visible. It is applied while the model generates text: it slightly shapes which tokens the model picks, so it adds no characters, markup, or hidden text to the response.

Detection is statistical. SpaceXSI scores a piece of text against the watermark and reports whether it is watermarked, not watermarked, or uncertain. Longer text gives a stronger signal.

Access to watermark detection is granted by application. You can submit a request for the detection API through this form.

## Opting out

Team admins can turn watermarking off for some or all models in the SpaceXSI Console. The setting applies to every API key on the team.

- Open the Team settings page and find the Model output watermarking row. It shows On (all models), Off (all models), or Custom. Only team admins see this row.
- Select the settings icon next to it, then clear the checkbox for each model you want to opt out. Select all turns every model on or off at once.
- Select Save. If you turned a model off, confirm with Opt Out.

Changes apply to new requests within 5 minutes. After you opt a model out, its new requests stop including the watermark; after you opt back in, they start including it again.

Opting out asks you to confirm that an exception under applicable law applies to your use, and that you are solely responsible for any marking, disclosure, or other legal requirement.

Some models may be locked on for your team. Locked models are listed in the dialog but cannot be turned off from the Console. To ask about a locked model, see Why can't I turn watermarking off for a model?

Every opt-in and opt-out is recorded in your team's audit log. Team admins can view it on the Audit Log page in the SpaceXSI Console. To find a change, search by event ID, description, or user, and use the time filter to narrow the results to a range of dates. For screenshots of these filters, see Do you have audit logs? in the security FAQ.

## FAQ

### Do I need to change my code?

No. Watermarking has no request parameter, and the response format is unchanged apart from thex-watermark header.

### Does opting out apply to all of my API keys?

Yes. The setting belongs to the team, so it applies to every API key on the team. You choose it separately for each model.

### Why can't I turn watermarking off for a model?

The model is locked on for your team. Locked models show in the watermarking dialog without a checkbox.

For questions about a locked model, contact your team admin. If you still have questions, email support@x.ai.

### Does watermarking affect quality or speed?

No. Watermarking doesn't change response quality or speed.

# xAI (Grok)

Thexai provider supports xAI's Grok models through an API interface compatible with OpenAI's format, including text, vision, image generation, video generation, and voice workflows.

## Setup

To use xAI's API, set theXAI_API_KEY environment variable or specify via apiKey in the configuration file.
export XAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here

When xAI is the selected fallback provider family, Promptfoo can use xAI defaults for grading, suggestions, synthesis, and web search. These automatic defaults currently usegrok-4.3 on the global endpoint; select grok-4.7, grok-4.6, or grok-4.5 explicitly where they are available. xAI does not currently expose a public embeddings or moderation API, so those defaults fall back to OpenAI when xAI is selected. Explicit provider IDs in your config still take precedence.

## Supported Models

The xAI provider includes support for the following model formats. xAI recommendsgrok-4.7 for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work; consult the public model catalog for current availability.

Legacy xAI model aliases

xAI periodically retires older model slugs and keeps them working through redirects. As of the May 15, 2026 (12:00 PM PT) retirement, requests to thegrok-4-1-fast, grok-4-fast, grok-4-0709, and grok-3 families redirect to grok-4.3 and use Grok 4.3 pricing. Requests to grok-code-fast-1 route to grok-build-0.1, while grok-imagine-image-pro routes to grok-imagine-image-quality. For new configs, use a current canonical model ID directly.

Regional model availability

xAI documents Grok 4.7 on its global and US regional endpoints, and announced Grok 4.5 availability in the EU API Console. Check your account before depending on Grok 4.7 in another region;grok-4.3 remains Promptfoo's automatic fallback.

### Grok 4.7 Models

- xai:grok-4.7 - Chat Completions; 500K context, text and image input, text output
- xai:responses:grok-4.7 - Responses API, including server-side tools and encrypted reasoning

Use the exactgrok-4.7 model ID. Grok 4.7 Fast is available in Cursor and Grok Build, but not on the public xAI API.

### Grok 4.6 Models

- xai:grok-4.6 - Previous flagship reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work (500K context, text and image input)

xAI does not publish any aliases for this model, so target the exactgrok-4.6 id. There is no grok-4.6-latest.

### Grok 4.5 Models

- xai:grok-4.5-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.5 family

- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent - Alias for the Grok 4.20 multi-agent family
- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.20 multi-agent family

### Grok 4.1 Fast Models

These legacy IDs remain recognized for backward compatibility and redirect to Grok 4.3:

- xai:grok-4-1-fast-reasoning and its -latest aliases - Redirect with low reasoning effort
- xai:grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning and its -latest aliases - Redirect with reasoning disabled

### Grok Code Fast Models

- xai:grok-build-0.1 - Canonical Grok Build coding model (256K context)
- xai:grok-code-fast-1 - Legacy alias that routes to grok-build-0.1
- xai:grok-code-fast - Alias for grok-build-0.1
- xai:grok-code-fast-1-0825 - Versioned alias for grok-build-0.1

### Grok-4 Fast Models

These legacy IDs remain recognized for backward compatibility and redirect to Grok 4.3:

- xai:grok-4-fast-reasoning and its aliases - Redirect with low reasoning effort
- xai:grok-4-fast-non-reasoning and its aliases - Redirect with reasoning disabled

### Grok-4 Models

- xai:grok-4-0709, xai:grok-4, and xai:grok-4-latest - Legacy IDs that redirect to Grok 4.3 with low reasoning effort

### Grok-3 Models

Thegrok-3, grok-3-beta, grok-3-fast, and related -latest IDs are legacy aliases that redirect to Grok 4.3. Promptfoo also recognizes the older Grok 3 Mini IDs for backward compatibility; verify their availability for your xAI account before relying on them.

### Grok-2 and previous Models

Promptfoo recognizes oldergrok-2, grok-beta, and vision IDs for existing configs, but they are not in xAI's current public catalog. Use a current model for new configs and verify legacy availability in the xAI Console.

## Configuration

The provider uses OpenAI-compatible configuration options plus Grok-specific options, subject to the model restrictions below. Example usage:

When xAI returnsusage.cost_in_usd_ticks, Promptfoo uses that exact billed amount, including cache discounts and request-level pricing adjustments. If ticks are unavailable, Promptfoo falls back to the model's catalog rates and applies the documented 2x premium when the response confirms service_tier: priority. Custom pricing can be set with cost, inputCost, outputCost, and cacheReadCost (all per-token rates); explicit overrides take precedence over reported ticks and are used as final rates without an additional priority multiplier.
providers:
  - id: xai:grok-4.7
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      reasoning_effort: 'xhigh' # low, medium, high (default), or xhigh
      apiKey: your_api_key_here # Alternative to XAI_API_KEY

Bothxai:<model> Chat Completions and xai:responses:<model> support xAI
Priority Processing.
Set service_tier to priority for higher scheduling priority or default for standard
processing; omitting it also uses the default tier. Other OpenAI-compatible tier names are not
valid on xAI.

### Reasoning Support

Multiple Grok models support reasoning capabilities:

Grok 4.7 and 4.6: Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to low, medium, high (the default), or xhigh. Responses API requests use reasoning.effort. Reasoning cannot be disabled; Promptfoo rejects none locally.

For Grok 4.7, cap output withmax_completion_tokens for Chat Completions or max_output_tokens for Responses. Chat also accepts max_tokens as an alias; use one spelling throughout an eval, including defaults and test cases. Within test options, set a request option directly or under passthrough, not both. Reasoning effort accepts a direct eval variable such as {{ effort }}; see the optional Grok 4.7 providers in the xAI chat example.

Grok 4.5: Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to low, medium, or high (the default); Promptfoo rejects other values locally. Responses API requests use reasoning.effort with the same values.

Grok 4.3: General-purpose reasoning model. Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to none, low, medium, or high; Responses API requests use reasoning.effort.

Grok Code Fast Models: Thegrok-code-fast-1 family are reasoning models optimized for agentic coding workflows. They support:

- Function calling and tool usage
- Web search viasearch_parameters
- Fast inference with built-in reasoning

### Grok 4.7 Specific Behavior

The xAI release notes list $2/M input, $0.50/M cached input, and $6/M output. At 200K or more input tokens, the rates are $4/M, $1/M, and $12/M respectively. When the API does not return a billed cost, Promptfoo uses these rates, including the 10% premium on xAI's US endpoint; explicit custom rates still take precedence. As with other Grok 4 reasoning models, Promptfoo stripspresence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop.

The Responses API returns encrypted reasoning even wheninclude is omitted. Promptfoo keeps it in response.raw.output; pass these items back unchanged when managing conversation history yourself.

### Grok 4.5 Specific Behavior

Grok 4.5 is an earlier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work:

- 500K context window with text and image input
- Configurable reasoning:reasoning_effort accepts low, medium, or high (defaults to high); none is rejected
- Long-context pricing: requests with at least 200K input tokens use the higher catalog rate ($4/M input, $0.60/M cached input, and $12/M output instead of $2/M, $0.30/M, and $6/M); Promptfoo uses the exact billed ticks when xAI returns them
- Unsupported parameters:presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop are rejected, and Promptfoo strips them automatically
- Ignored parameters: xAI silently ignoreslogprobs and top_logprobs on Grok 4.20 and newer models
- Server-side tools: usexai:responses:grok-4.5 for web search, X search, code execution, and MCP

    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      reasoning_effort: medium
      max_completion_tokens: 4096

### Grok 4.3 Specific Behavior

Grok 4.3 is a general-purpose alternative for text workflows:

- Configurable reasoning: Setreasoning_effort to none, low, medium, or high

# One nation under Grok

### News notes from the last 48 hours

##### Foreword

The Pope’s advice was pretty sound this week where it mattered most. How can we get Grok to convert to Catholicism?

#### Trump “consulted Grok — but not Congress,” say House Democrats demanding preservation of chat logs

They seem to have read an early October story in TIME that revealed Trump had come to see Grok as a genius after the raid to capture Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro.

A source told TIME that Grok had told Trump before the invasion that Venezuelans would likely celebrate the capture. Celebrations were indeed part of the post-abduction landscape.

This exchange was part of a December 2025 meeting between Trump and Elon Musk in which “Trump spent hours asking Grok questions about his presidency and legacy.”

#### Pope Leo vaguely advises against building superhuman AI

Indirectly but ambiguously alluding to things to be avoided is a longstanding tradition in Christian preaching, but I wish he would just say, “For the love of God, don’t build superhuman AI using anything like current methods.”

Instead, he tweeted, “A reliable system that serves the human person is of greater value than one that is exceptionally powerful but whose consequences cannot be adequately foreseen or controlled.”

Amen?

#### Maybe we’ll need to rebuild much of the internet every few months

It would be a logical extension of Alex Stamos’s suggestion on the Galaxy Brain podcast this week. With open-weight AI models letting “a 19-year-old in St. Petersburg” with a high-end Mac do work that used to take a team of hundreds, pre-AI code is looking like Swiss cheese. Stamos endorses companies rewriting their legacy code bases in more secure languages, something AI is very good at.

But I think it remains to be seen just how good; if later models can still find holes in this newer code, the process might have to be repeated every so often.

Will there be time? Epoch AI reported that open-weight models are now strong enough to discern and exploit flaws addressed by early-release patches before those patches are widely rolled out. For about $1,000 a pop, researchers were able to create zero-click exploits that would impact visiting users of the Firefox browser who hadn’t yet installed pending patches.

Meanwhile, our so-called “black October” cyber crisis hit a new milestone Thursday, with North Korean hackers stealing $6.3 billion from cryptocurrency exchange Binance. This is by far the largest crypto heist ever. To no one’s surprise, “thousands of transactions in a short period suggest that the attackers are using automation.”

#### Rented compute is a massive loophole in U.S. export restrictions

China can rent almost as much computing power from Southeast Asian data centers that can legally buy high-end American AI chips as exists in all of mainland China.

There could be a silver lining to this, I suppose: The potential to halve China’s AI compute with a diplomatic stroke could provide leverage in international negotiations to stop the race to superhuman AI.

一个事实，刘大一恒这次是出了新手村，就要面对大魔（模）王。姚顺雨在当今全国，乃至全球AI圈的地位无需多言。

2026年5月，马化腾曾这么评价腾讯AI：“原来一年前我们以为上了船，后来发现那个船漏水了，现在感觉站上去了，还坐不下去，还是希望船速能快一点。”

10月的时候，广东省领导来到腾讯总部调研座谈，姚顺雨就坐在马化腾身边。看来姚顺雨已经将这艘原本“漏水的船”，修得让马化腾坐得下去了。。

刘大一恒能取胜吗？

## 01

现在下结论还太早，但可以确定的是，刘大一恒不能输。

过去腾讯和阿里的竞争，更多发生在产品、云和生态上。从钉钉与企业微信，到千问办公与WorkBuddy。两家公司争夺的是入口，比如谁能进入企业的工作流程，谁就有机会把AI变成真正的生产力。

但在旗舰基座模型上，双方始终差着一个身位。这种错频，也让两边有足够的空间去叙事。

阿里可以讲Qwen的模型能力、开源生态和全球开发者，腾讯则可以讲混元如何接入元宝、CodeBuddy、WorkBuddy，如何利用自己的产品场景反馈模型。

双方并非没有竞争，只是从没有在同一时间，用同一代正式旗舰，正面PK。

火药味是从8月底开始传出来的。

8月26日，阿里发布Qwen3.8-Flash-Next，提前展示Qwen4架构。8月28日，腾讯发布并开源Hy4 preview。

两次发布只隔两天，也都把Agent和真实生产力放在重要位置。

但这只是预览版之间的试探，而且当时刘大一恒尚未以Qwen新负责人的身份公开亮相，因此还不能算他与姚顺雨的正面对决。

就相当于在比武之前，双方互相秀了秀起手式，看谁马步扎得更稳。

到了Qwen4和Hy4，同为主力数字代际，刘大一恒和姚顺雨同样背负各自组织调整后的压力。两个人将第一次被市场放进同一个坐标系里。

刘大一恒是阿里内部一路拼出来的人。

2021年加入达摩院后，他就是Qwen早期核心成员，长期负责预训练，之后职责扩展到后训练和Coding，也参与过多模态、数学等模型研发。

刘大一恒在姚顺雨面前是个“新”人，因为这是刘大一恒第一次要对这个模型的整体结果负责。

以前只要把预训练做好就算完成了KPI，现在开始，他要把架构、后训练、Agent能力、开源叙事一切都扛起来。

林俊旸离开之后，阿里需要的不单单是一个模型，还要让市场知道，Qwen的体系至今依然能够稳定运转。

姚顺雨和刘大一恒完全相反。他是带着最顶级的履历空降到混元的。

他是ReAct和Tree of Thoughts（思维树）的共同提出者、OpenAI前研究员，还参与过OpenAI的Operator、Deep Research等项目。

姚顺雨来到腾讯以后，重建预训练和强化学习基础设施，调整研发组织，把模型与产品反馈连接起来。到2026年7月，混元多模态模型部门与大语言模型部门又合并为基础模型部，由姚顺雨统一管理。

Hy4正是在这样的背景下诞生的，这个模型是一个完全贯彻姚顺雨意志的产品。

刘大一恒的首战之所以难，不光是因为姚顺雨名气大，更是因为姚顺雨已经把个人研究能力，转化成了组织能力。

当然了，姚顺雨同样需要Hy4正式版回答，视觉与Agent能否真正结合？全链路RSI到底能带来多少性能提升？腾讯庞大的产品体系又能否持续反哺模型？

## 02

聊完人，再回到模型本身。Qwen4与Hy4都不是毫无铺垫的新品，双方在预览版里已经亮出了一部分底牌。

先看Qwen4。它最大的看点，是新架构第一次接受旗舰级检验。

阿里将Qwen3.8-Flash-Next明确定义为Qwen4架构的早期预览。

这个模型在注意力机制中结合Gated DeltaNet（GDN）与Qwen Sparse Attention（QSA），同时引入门控残差、N-gram Embedding和Muon优化器。

第一个看点是智能水平。

按阿里披露，它的主干为125B参数，另有51B N-gram Embedding，每个Token激活6B参数，训练成本仅为Qwen3.7-Plus的九分之一。

刘大一恒非常在意“每一份算力到底能够换来多少智能？”

算力紧缺是所有国产AI的通病，一旦用更低成本换来更多的智能水平，那么模型的智能水平直接“起飞”。

此前，新架构先在Flash上验证了可行性。到了Qwen4这里，它要回答的是，这套架构能否延续到Max上。

因为Max通常要处理更大规模和更复杂的任务，往往轻量模型能成立的事情，到了几万亿参数的模型上，很容易失效。

如果它只能做出便宜的小模型，却不能提高旗舰智能上限，那就说明刘大一恒还是差点意思。

第二个看点是真实Agent。

刘大一恒在云栖大会上的演讲题目就是《Qwen：迈向真实世界智能体》。真实世界四个字很重要，因为Agent不能只会在演示里连续调用几次工具，而要在长任务里记住目标、处理上下文、使用工具、纠正错误，最后交付可以直接使用的代码、文档或分析结果。

Qwen4的提升如果只能体现在单轮问答，而没有体现在长程任务的成功率上，就很难支撑阿里对真实生产力的叙事。

第三个看点，也是Qwen4最特别的一条线，RSI。

刘大一恒在云栖大会上表示，Qwen3.8-Max已经能够在人类几乎“零参与”的条件下，自主搭建训练流程、构造训练数据、设计实验并定位缺陷，持续迭代超过一个月，完成33轮有效迭代。

根据阿里的数据，其Artificial Analysis评测得分从40提升到了45。

刘大一恒表示，RSI还从模型训练延伸到了推理与芯片。模型自主适配平头哥新款架构后，推理框架单实例吞吐量提升96%。在芯片协同设计中，模型仅依据总线模块规范，经过60小时自迭代和超过一万次EDA工具调用，将物理实现面积缩减42%。

他把这个关系概括为：“模型设计芯片，而更强的芯片又将反哺更强的模型。”

再看Hy4。腾讯表示，这次注重的是强化长程和真实生产力任务能力，显著提升思维链效率，并首次引入视觉理解。

前两项，就是阿里腾讯对决的核心，相当于两个人谁的拳头大，谁的胳膊粗。

视觉理解是Hy4一个重要变化。

毕竟现实中的工作并不只有纯文本，还有截图、图表、PDF版面、网页和软件界面这些多模态元素。

首次引入视觉理解之后，Hy4能否从“读懂任务”走向“看懂工作现场”，并把视觉、工具调用与长程执行连起来，是它与Hy3的重要区别。

同时，这次混元也破天荒地推出了Hy4 Flash，负责性价比和规模化调用的任务。

腾讯表示，Hy4 Flash将继承Hy4的视觉、Agent能力，并通过模型与产品的深度Co-Design高频进化。

这意味着腾讯不只想要一个高分旗舰，也想把能力下放到WorkBuddy、CodeBuddy等更高频的真实场景里。

虽然严格来说，这不是腾讯混元历史上第一次分档。早在2024年，腾讯云就开放过hunyuan-pro、hunyuan-standard和hunyuan-lite，后来还有Turbo。HY2的Think与Instruct，也分别对应推理和指令版本。

Hy4 Flash的第一次，是指姚顺雨重建后，首次在同一代明确形成“旗舰＋Flash”的双档布局。

阿里和腾讯已经来到了八角笼内，而八角笼内，什么都有可能发生。

# Apple Intelligence to roll out on iPhones in China in December with Alibaba backing

Alibaba’s flagship AI model Qwen will be integrated into Apple Intelligence, after years of speculation and regulatory uncertainty

2-MIN READ2-MIN

0

Listen

Ann Caoin Shanghai

Apple’s long-awaited artificial intelligence features will be officially launched in China in December, ending two years of regulatory uncertainty as the US tech giant seeks to bring advanced technologies to its second-largest market with the help of Alibaba Group Holding.

The first batch of Apple Intelligence services will roll out to Chinese iPhone users alongside the iOS 27.3 update in December, following an open beta test with developers starting November 4, the US company said in a statement on Saturday.

The initial roll-out will include around 18 new features provided by Apple Intelligence, including writing tools for summarising and proofreading, live translation for phone calls and messages, as well as visual intelligence via camera controls, according to the statement.

However, Chinese users will not have the same access as those in many international markets, as Apple noted that its latest Siri AI capabilities and other next-generation AI services, launched by the company in September, would be excluded from this initial release. Siri is the virtual assistant across Apple’s ecosystem.

The statement did not specify when Apple Intelligence would be available to users of other Apple devices in China.

Notably, Alibaba’s flagship AI model Qwen will be integrated into Apple Intelligence through a partnership between the two firms that allows users to prompt Qwen for text generation, image creation, as well as photo or document analysis via Siri.

“We are delighted to cooperate with Apple,” said Eddie Wu Yongming, chief executive officer of Alibaba, in a statement on Saturday. “Qwen will draw on Alibaba’s deep AI technology stack to deeply integrate into the Apple ecosystem, jointly delivering entirely new intelligent experiences for Apple users in China.”

Alibaba owns the South China Morning Post.

The launch came after Apple faced years of regulatory headwinds in bringing its AI services to its second-largest market. While Apple Intelligence was launched in the US and other international markets in 2024, China’s cyberspace rules require generative AI models deployed in the country to pass rigorous safety reviews by the country’s internet watchdog.

In July, Chinese regulators granted Apple the long-awaited licence to roll out AI services on iPhones in the country, alongside six other smartphone-based AI services, including those for Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies.

## DEV Community

This edition of the Model Releases Digest covers what's new from 2026-10-17 through 2026-10-31: a new frontier leader from Google DeepMind, a brand-new category of interactive world model, a cheaper fast-tier model from OpenAI, a near-frontier model from Moonshot AI about to go open weight, and a trillion-parameter open-weight drop from Mistral.

## 🔥 Highlights

Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model — new #1 model, built for cyber defense

We're announcing Genie 4, our new world model for real-time interactive simulation — real-time interactive worlds with native audio

Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra — faster, cheaper computer-use at frontier quality

Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro — near-frontier scores, open weights coming soon

Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) is now open weight — trillion-parameter frontier model, now fully open

## Anthropic news

Nothing relevant this cycle — the items published since 2026-10-17 were partnerships, policy, and safety-research posts (including a distillation-defenses writeup), with no new Claude model version, pricing change, or capability update.

## OpenAI news

Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra — 2026-10-26. OpenAI's new fast, cost-efficient multimodal model succeeds GPT-5.6 Terra, pricing 50% below both GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol while scoring 15 points higher than its predecessor on the "Agents' Last Exam" benchmark at roughly a third of the cost. Practical value: it matches GPT-6 Astra's computer-use quality at a tenth of the price, making high-volume visual-reasoning and computer-use automation dramatically cheaper to run.

## Google DeepMind / Google AI blog

Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model — 2026-10-28. Built on Gemini 4 Argon, Carbon now ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with big jumps in coding, agentic, and long-horizon tasks (teams report runs lasting days on complex engineering problems), plus state-of-the-art cybersecurity-defense scores. Rollout is initially gated to cyber defenders and safety-program partners before wider availability, with pricing held at $2/M input and $10/M output tokens — same as Argon.

We're announcing Genie 4, our new world model for real-time interactive simulation — 2026-10-27. Genie 4 generates real-time, steerable interactive simulations with native on-the-fly audio (ambient sound, music, dialogue), built on Gemini for visual realism and scene coherence. It's rolling out to a limited set of testers now, with wider access for Google AI Ultra and Gemini API partners coming soon — framed both as a training ground for robots/agents and as a new creative tool for film, journalism, and game development.

## Meta AI blog

Nothing new — Meta's blog listing hasn't been updated since July 2026; the newest visible post is still "Introducing Muse Spark 1.1."

## Mistral news

Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) is now open weight — 2026-10-29. After three additional weeks of RL since its earlier preview, Mistral is releasing open weights for its trillion-parameter, natively multimodal Large 4, now leading open-weight benchmarks in coding (FrontierCode, Terminal-Bench) and defensive cybersecurity, with three reasoning modes for cost/performance tradeoffs. Practical value: a frontier-scale model that's fully self-hostable, a meaningful option for sovereign-AI and compliance-sensitive deployments in the EU and beyond.

Voxtral 3: Speech-to-Text, TTS & Voice Agents — 2026-10-20. Mistral's third-generation voice stack adds a full voice-agent SDK alongside new speech-to-text and TTS models supporting real-time, multi-turn conversation across 50+ languages with emotionally adaptive synthesis. It's available via Mistral's EU-hosted API or self-deployment, giving teams a sovereign alternative to proprietary real-time voice-agent platforms.

## Hugging Face blog

Build specialized multimodal models with LFM3 — 2026-10-27. Liquid AI's LFM3 family puts text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models on one shared 2B-class backbone; the 1.7B variant outperforms the previous LFM2.5-2.6B with 35% fewer parameters, fits in ~1GB at 4-bit quantization, and supports a 256K context window. Practical value: a smaller, cheaper, single-GPU-finetunable family for on-device agents across five modalities instead of one large MoE.

Granite Switch 4.1.1 — Update models like you update software — 2026-10-29. This patch release on Granite Switch 4.1 swaps in an updated multilingual speech-recognition adapter (10 languages, native punctuation/casing) and an improved decision adapter onto the same base checkpoint, with no retraining required. Practical value: it demonstrates IBM's adapter-swap deployment pattern — shipping capability updates without redeploying or retraining the base model.

## Simon Willison

Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra — 2026-10-26. Simon's independent writeup frames GPT-6.1 Terra as sitting in the Sonnet-equivalent price/capability slot — cheaper than GPT-6.1 Sol, smarter than Luna — and notes OpenAI's own comparison to Astra/Sol on vision and computer-use quality at much higher speed. Practical value for readers: a clear read on where Terra lands in OpenAI's own pricing ladder, beyond the official announcement's benchmark claims.

Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro — 2026-10-23. Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro is live on the API now, with open weights promised by November 4, 2026, priced at $2/$10 per million tokens — half of Claude Opus 5.5. It scored 55 on the Artificial Analysis index, ahead of Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon (all at 53) and behind only Opus 5.5 (58), making it the first soon-to-be-open-weight model to score this close to the frontier.

## Through-line

Three independent signals point the same direction this cycle: the frontier keeps climbing (Gemini 4 Carbon's agentic and cybersecurity gains), the cost of near-frontier capability keeps collapsing (GPT-6.1 Terra's 50% price cut, Kimi K3.1 Pro undercutting Opus 5.5 at near-matching scores), and the open-weight tier keeps closing the gap almost immediately after each closed release (Mistral Large 4's open-weighting, Kimi K3.1 Pro's upcoming weight drop, LFM3 pushing multimodal capability down to edge-sized models). Add Genie 4's debut of real-time interactive world simulation as a genuinely new product category, and this feels less like incremental iteration and more like several fronts moving at once.

# Gemini 4 Carbon: Google's #1 AI Model, and the Release Strategy That Matters More Than the Score

Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28, 2026 — its second frontier model in a single month — and it immediately took the top spot on the independently run Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 with a score of 59. But the more interesting story for builders is not the one-point lead. It is how Google is releasing it: defenders first, everyone else eventually.

## What Carbon Is

Carbon is Google DeepMind's newest proprietary frontier model, positioned as the stronger successor to Gemini 4 Argon (launched two weeks earlier). Google's framing: "our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities." Internal teams reportedly ran it for days at a time on multi-step engineering tasks — the pitch is sustained autonomous engineering work, not just smarter chat.

The composite index numbers:

- Gemini 4 Carbon (high): 59
- Claude Opus 5.5 (max): 58
- GPT-6 Astra (max): 57
- Gemini 4 Argon: 50

A nine-point jump over Argon and a one-point composite lead over Opus 5.5. But composite wins hide task-level losses: Carbon scores 59 vs 62 for Opus 5.5 on the AA Coding Agent Index, and trails Kimi K3.1 Pro, Muse Wonder, and Grok 4.7 on AA-Briefcase. Best composite doesn't mean best at every job.

## The Security Scores

The launch is framed around cybersecurity, and Google ran the security benchmarks without guardrails — itself a signal of why access is restricted:

- 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro (finding vulnerabilities)
- 54.8% on ExploitGym (exploiting them)
- 71.0% on CWE-bench (patching to root cause)

The honest caveats: these are Google's own numbers, unreproduced by independent parties (The Decoder's reporting), and defenders using the safeguarded version will be working with a different system. Google also says Terminal-Bench 4.0 cheating collapsed to 0.0% successful / 0.4% attempted — evaluation integrity improving while accuracy rises.

## Pricing and Access

The model to actually build on today is still Argon. But the deeper signal is the release pattern: frontier capability now ships with staged, defender-first access and government pre-release review. If you plan products around frontier models, start designing for staged access now — this looks like the template.

# Soika Labs Launches Mockingjay Network, an Agentic AI Operating System That Lets Businesses Command Their Own AI Workforce

Unveiled at the Dubai AI Festival, the desktop-first platform lets businesses build, deploy and connect AI agents across a global network with early-access UAE users receiving 5,000 free credits.

Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 31st October 2026, ZEX PR WIRE — Soika Labs has opened early access to Mockingjay Network, an agentic AI operating system that lets any business build, run and command its own workforce of AI agents. Co-founder and CEO Enzo Amur unveiled the platform’s move into production at the Dubai AI Festival on 27 October, launching with a UAE-first soft rollout that gives early-access users 5,000 free credits to start building.

One platform where AI agents work as a team

An AI agent is a digital worker software that carries out real business tasks such as answering customers, qualifying and sorting leads, or standing up an entire CRM system. Most AI tools, however, operate in isolation, leaving teams to pay for several products and stitch the results together by hand. Mockingjay Network brings all of that into a single environment. Inside a company, agents work together as a coordinated team; beyond it, they connect with agents from other organisations worldwide through the Global Agentic Neural Network (GANN) to get work done faster. Each company’s private agents stay sovereign, plugging into the wider network without exposing internal data.

No code, your models, your machines

Mockingjay is built to be used without writing a line of code or hiring engineers, and it can run on a company’s own computers so sensitive data stays under its control. The platform is also one of the largest LLM aggregators available, giving users access to Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude, Kimi and more from a single place. An intelligent auto-routing system directs each task to the best-suited model saving up to 70% of credits while agents work across text, images and data. Mockingjay is delivered as a desktop application that businesses install and run locally.

Built for small and medium businesses first

Mockingjay is designed for small and medium-sized businesses before anyone else, and the opportunity is vast: an estimated 1.3 million SMEs in the UAE, around 2 million across the wider GCC, and some 36.2 million small businesses in the United States. Many want to adopt AI but find it too expensive or too complicated. Mockingjay is built to close that gap, bringing agentic AI within practical reach of leaner teams.

People stay in command

For all its automation, Mockingjay is designed around human oversight. Soika Labs sets a baseline of at least one person per division and expects “human in the loop” to become a profession of its own as businesses scale. “The rules of communication, cooperation and equality between AI agents are what make a shared network work,” said Enzo Amur, Co-founder and CEO of Soika Labs. “We want businesses to let AI do more so people can be more without letting AI take over.” The launch aligns with the UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031, as businesses across the region move from adopting AI tools to applying them for measurable operational value.

Availability and early access

Mockingjay Network is available now as a desktop application. Businesses can download it and start building their AI agents and fleets at https://www.mockingjaynetwork.com/download. As part of the UAE-first soft launch, early-access users receive 5,000 free credits. “This is the beginning of a network where businesses of every size build their own AI workforce and connect it to the world,” added Amur.

About Soika Labs

Soika Labs is a Dubai-based AI company and the team behind Mockingjay Network. Built on the principle that in the era of AI being human matters more, it develops agentic AI infrastructure that keeps businesses and people in control.

# QwikBuild’s $2.3 Million Bet: Can AI Agents Turn Enterprise Software Development into a Faster, More Accessible Process?

Enterprise software development has traditionally been a long process involving product managers, designers, engineers, testers, infrastructure specialists and multiple rounds of review. Even relatively contained applications can take months to move from requirements to deployment, particularly when they must connect to existing systems or meet enterprise security standards.

Bengaluru-based QwikBuild is betting that AI agents can compress much of that process. The startup raised $2.3 million in a pre-seed round led by Japan-listed Globalway, with participation from Blume Ventures, DeVC, Marsshot and angel investors including Groww founder Lalit Keshre and Curefoods CEO Ankit Nagori, according to Inc42’s October 28 report.

The funding is notable for two reasons. It gives an early-stage Indian enterprise AI startup capital to expand its go-to-market efforts, and it arrives alongside a joint venture with Globalway to enter Japan’s enterprise software market. The combination of product ambition and an overseas distribution partnership makes QwikBuild a useful signal of where the enterprise AI startup market is heading.

## From a prompt to a working software product

QwikBuild’s product proposition is built around AgentQ, an AI-led system intended to take a software idea towards a deployed application. On its website, the company describes a workflow in which a user explains the product they want, a product-management agent turns the request into a build plan, and specialised agents handle backend development, frontend development and code review.

The company says human developers remain part of the process for complex integrations, payment gateways and architecture reviews. The product is therefore not presented simply as a chatbot that writes code. It is an attempt to coordinate multiple software-development tasks through agents, with engineers available where judgement and specialist intervention are required.

That distinction matters. Generating a code snippet is relatively easy to demonstrate. Building a reliable application requires requirements discovery, system design, data modelling, integration, testing, security, deployment and ongoing maintenance. The commercial opportunity lies in orchestrating enough of that lifecycle to reduce time and complexity without compromising reliability.

## The market opportunity is larger than faster coding

Many businesses need software that is too specific for an off-the-shelf product but too small or specialised to justify a large custom-development programme. Internal portals, workflow tools, booking systems, customer applications and operational dashboards often sit in this gap.

If an AI-led development platform can make these applications faster and less expensive to build, it could expand the number of businesses able to commission custom software. It may also help larger enterprises prototype internal tools, modernise legacy workflows or build specialised interfaces around existing systems.

But the economics will depend on more than development speed. Buyers need predictable costs, secure deployment, maintainable code, clear ownership of intellectual property and confidence that applications will continue to work as business requirements change. Enterprise software is judged by what happens after launch, not just how quickly the first version appears.

QwikBuild says its platform provides a dedicated database, enterprise security, one-click deployment and code that customers own. These are important claims for its target market, but they will need to be tested in real deployments, particularly where applications handle sensitive data or connect to mission-critical systems.

## Why the Globalway partnership matters

The joint venture with Globalway gives QwikBuild a route into Japan’s enterprise software market. For an early-stage startup, international expansion can be difficult without local customer access, language support, implementation partners and an understanding of enterprise procurement. A partner with an established presence can help bridge some of those gaps.

Japan is an interesting market for this proposition. Many organisations are under pressure to modernise legacy systems and improve software productivity, while enterprise buyers tend to place high importance on reliability, security and implementation support. Those requirements can make the market attractive but demanding for a young software company.

The partnership will need to demonstrate that QwikBuild can adapt its product and delivery model to local enterprise needs. A joint venture announcement is a route to market, not proof of customer adoption. The next evidence will be paying customers, repeat usage and applications that move beyond pilots into sustained business operations.

## The agentic software development race is getting crowded

QwikBuild is entering a fast-moving category. Large model providers are improving coding capabilities, developer platforms are embedding AI assistants into existing workflows, and startups are building systems that coordinate agents across planning, coding, testing and deployment.

This creates a difficult strategic question: where does a specialised platform retain an advantage when the underlying models and coding tools are widely available?

One possible answer is workflow orchestration. Enterprises do not necessarily want a collection of disconnected AI tools. They want a process that understands requirements, manages dependencies, applies organisational standards, checks output and produces software that can be operated safely. Another potential advantage is human support: real engineers who can resolve difficult architectural and integration problems may be valuable to customers who cannot rely on autonomous code generation alone.

Yet both advantages are operationally intensive. If every complex project requires substantial human intervention, the platform may struggle to deliver the economics implied by rapid, automated development. If it removes too much human review, quality and security risks can rise. Finding the right balance is central to the business model.

## What the new capital needs to prove

The $2.3 million pre-seed round is intended to support go-to-market expansion, including building a US team and growing across Southeast Asia, alongside the Japan joint venture. For a startup at this stage, the immediate priority should be proving a repeatable customer problem and a repeatable way to solve it.

Several indicators will matter more than the number of agents in the product. How many applications reach production? How often do customers return to build additional software? What proportion of projects can be completed without extensive engineering intervention? How much post-launch maintenance is required? And can the platform meet enterprise expectations around access controls, audit trails, data protection and software ownership?

The strongest evidence will be a customer who can point to a business process that previously required a lengthy custom-development project and now runs reliably through software built with the platform.

QwikBuild’s funding and Globalway partnership capture a larger shift in enterprise AI: the ambition is moving from helping people write code to changing how software is specified, assembled and delivered. That is a much bigger market, but also a much harder one to win.

For Indian startups, the opportunity is not simply to build another coding assistant. It is to create trusted systems that can take responsibility for meaningful parts of the software lifecycle. QwikBuild has raised its first institutional capital to pursue that opportunity. The next milestone is proving that speed can translate into dependable enterprise software and repeatable revenue.
